commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Emit self-describing events for recurrent state groups
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` emits a `block_size=0` placeholder `BlockStored` for every group that has a load window. `MambaSpec` groups get a one-chunk window because they depend on a single state, not because their hashes are meaningless: the offloaded chunk is the recurrent state checkpoint at the chunk's last hash. External consumers that index offload residency (a KV-aware router with a CPU/KVCR tier) therefore cannot see where a hybrid prefix is reusable and overestimate it from the attention group (vllm-project/vllm#62510).

## Changes

- `events.py`: `describes_group()` returns true for full-attention and `MambaSpec` groups; windowed attention groups keep the placeholder.
- A recurrent chunk (or partial tail) is announced as **one state checkpoint**: `block_hashes` is the chunk's last hash only, `parent_block_hash` is the hash before it, `token_ids` is empty, `kv_cache_spec_kind="mamba"`, `group_idx` and `block_size` as for attention. `BlockRemoved` fans out to that same single hash. Consumers align it by hash with the attention group's blocks; announcing the whole hash range would let them treat every hash in a multi-hash chunk as a resumable position. The payload is also small: no per-chunk `token_ids` copy is retained for recurrent groups.
- Tests: Mamba chunk store/remove, a multi-hash (chunk-mode) chunk announcing only its last hash, and partial tail (store and lookup); windowed groups still skip.
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`: one sentence.

## Test plan

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py`: 51 passed in a CPU-only `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` container with this `events.py` dropped in; the 4 tiering-config tests in that file fail there identically without the patch (`VllmConfig` hybrid-KV-manager validation in that environment), so they need the CI environment.
- Qwen3.5-4B, `mamba_cache_mode=align`, `CPUOffloadingSpec` + `self_describing_kv_events`, ZMQ subscriber: before, the three SSM groups publish only `block_size=0` events; after, they publish one `kv_cache_spec_kind=mamba` event per chunk carrying the chunk's last hash, at the same hash as the attention group's chunk (table in the first comment; re-run on the checkpoint-only payload pending).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Preserve multimodal processor-cache hits during request eviction
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Prevent `AssertionError: Expected a cached item` when a multimodal request exceeds the processor-only LRU capacity. Retain requested payload references before inserting misses, so an earlier insert cannot discard a later hit.

Related #26195. This differs from #34749, which converts cache assertions into request errors without preserving the evicted payload. No open PR implementing request-local processor-only retention was found.

## Claims

- Requests such as `[new C, cached A, cached B]` succeed with a cache that holds only two images.
- Retained tensors, prompt updates, image ordering and repeated-image placeholders match uncached processing exactly.
- Payload lookups use constant-time `LRUCache.peek()`, which leaves eviction order and hit statistics unchanged. No cache-wide dictionary or tensor copies are made.
- Metadata-only and shared-memory sender behavior and the LRU storage budget are preserved.

## Validation

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tested base `fb7def9ef9`, real LLaVA CPU processor | All three eviction-order regressions fail with `AssertionError: Expected a cached item` |
| Updated branch, CPU | Nine LRU/processor checks and six existing IPC, shared-memory eviction and oversized-item checks pass |
| Preceding head `0cdb70d572a9`, H200 MIG 35GB | The new `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression passed in [Buildkite #98285](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98285#01a187b5-57c0-4e8f-82d1-9427bb7940e1); relevant multimodal jobs also passed in [Buildkite #98389](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98389). Its unrelated P2P failure is fixed by #64555, included in the rebased branch |
| Earlier v0.30.0 Kimi backport, TP8/DCP8/PP2, eight API servers, 8 MiB processor cache | 48/48 cache-pressure responses returned HTTP 200 with correct image order and complete SSE; the original processor reproduced the assertion |
| Earlier Kimi backport with DSpark K=3 and CPU offload | Full endpoint suite passed; accepted speculative-token delta 7,630; both PP pods retained UIDs, readiness and zero restarts |

Fresh full CI: [Buildkite #98475](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98475) is running on rebased head `a5111456ec1a`, based on main `4b47db922b83`. Both patch commits are unchanged after rebase (`git range-diff`); local checks and pre-commit passed again.

The new `peek` test verifies payload identity, stored `None`, missing-key defaults, unchanged hit statistics and eviction of the original oldest entry. It fails with `AttributeError` on the base runtime, which lacks `peek`.

CPU test commands, from a vLLM/test environment:

```sh
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' \
  tests/utils_/test_cache.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -k 'lru_cache or processor_cache_preserves_hits_when_request_exceeds_capacity or (processing_correctness and llava-1.5-7b-hf)' -q --tb=short

env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' tests/multimodal/test_cache.py \
  -k 'ipc_enable_disable_consistency or oversized_item_is_served_uncached or cache_eviction_lru_cache or cache_eviction_shm_cache' -q --tb=short
```

Results on rebased head `a5111456ec1a`: `9 passed, 515 deselected`; `6 passed, 24 deselected`. Local execution used an existing uv-managed Python 3.12.11 environment. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy, Ruff, markdownlint and test tethering.

To reproduce the original failure, run the added processor regression against the base runtime:

```sh
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processor_cache_preserves_hits_when_request_exceeds_capacity -q --tb=short
```

Base output, for each of the three orders:

```text
vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py:428: in get_and_update_item
    assert mm_item is not None, f"Expected a cached item for {mm_hash=}"
E   AssertionError: Expected a cached item for mm_hash='...'
```

The GPU regression launches real LLaVA weights with two API servers, a two-image cache and prefix caching disabled. It keeps requests on one HTTP connection and compares the pressure request's prompt count and token logprobs with a cold-cache reference. Buildkite selects the processor, utility and endpoint tests and covers their changed source files.

The earlier Kimi endpoint suite covered complete nonempty 512-token SSE, cached prompt logprobs, single/multiple images, tools and roundtrip, code execution, reasoning, long context, French/Arabic, creative output, memory, spatial vision, 80 load requests at concurrency 8/32, and 26 constrained JSON requests plus four ordinary companions. Normal responses were manually inspected and coherent. Neither PP pod logged grammar rejections, engine deaths, CUDA/NCCL errors or tracebacks during those tests. That run validates the original retention backport; the new lookup refinement has not been deployed to Kimi.

### Lookup performance

The previous accessor constructed `_MappingOrderCacheView`, whose `UserDict` constructor copied every cache entry for each requested item. The review refinement replaces this with a direct lookup in the LRU's backing dictionary.

Measured on macOS arm64, Python 3.12.11, cachetools 7.2.6. Times are medians of five samples; each sample performs 20 old lookups or 50,000 `peek` lookups. Temporary allocation is traced separately.

| Cache entries | Previous lookup | `peek` lookup | Previous temporary allocation | `peek` temporary allocation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | 49.50 µs | 0.039 µs | 39,152 B | 0 B |
| 10,000 | 532.36 µs | 0.037 µs | 311,536 B | 0 B |
| 100,000 | 6,354.41 µs | 0.039 µs | 5,767,408 B | 0 B |

This is a lookup microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput or capacity measurement.

<details>
<summary>Lookup timing reproduction</summary>

```sh
env -u UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER uv --no-config run --no-project --python 3.12 --with cachetools python - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
import statistics
import timeit

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("cache", "vllm/utils/cache.py")
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
for count in (1_000, 10_000, 100_000):
    cache = module.LRUCache(count)
    for index in range(count):
        cache.put(str(index), index)
    key = str(count // 2)
    for name, lookup, number in (
        ("previous", lambda: cache.cache.get(key), 20),
        ("peek", lambda: cache.peek(key), 50_000),
    ):
        samples = timeit.repeat(lookup, number=number, repeat=5)
        print(count, name, statistics.median(samples) / number * 1e6, "us")
PY
```

</details>

## Details

Touching all requested hashes cannot protect every hit when a request's working set exceeds the cache budget. Inserting C can evict A even though A was classified as cached before processing; the merge then supplies `None` for A and asserts.

Snapshot requested local payload references before inserts, using `LRUCache.peek()` without changing eviction order or statistics. If a hit is subsequently evicted, supply the retained tensor/update tuple through the existing insertion path. Sender caches inherit a local lookup returning `None` and keep their existing behavior.

The request-local dictionary and references last through the merge. The LRU remains bounded, but tensors needed by an in-flight request can outlive their cache entries; the optimization guide documents this transient memory. No tensors are copied, and there are no model-runner, scheduler, GPU encoder-cache or speculative-decoding changes.

Earlier Kimi validation used the pinned v0.30.0 image, TP8/DCP8/PP2, DSpark K=3 and eight API servers. CPU offload used 128 GiB/rank and 12,000 eager blocks, with actual PP0/PP1 pools of 69.21/103.82 GiB per rank. Offload behavior is unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Build run-batch TypeAdapters once instead of per request
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `vllm run-batch` builds a new pydantic `TypeAdapter` for each `/v1/embeddings`, `/score` and fallback input line, and for each `JSONResponse` it converts back. Each build regenerates the core schema, which costs about 0.5 ms. This PR builds the four adapters once at module level. ## Claims - In the current run-batch flow, the per-line frontend cost for an embeddings batch drops from 1,952 µs to 178 µs (~11×, median of 3 runs). For a 1.45M-line batch, single-threaded frontend CPU time drops from about 47 min to about 4.3 min. - The event-loop ceiling of `run_one_request` rises from about 800 to about 6,600 req/s. - Behavior does not change. Parsed bodies, validation errors (type, loc and msg), and converted responses are identical before and after. ## Validation **Regression test.** `test_requests_and_responses_reuse_type_adapters` wraps `TypeAdapter` in a spy, parses embeddings, score and fallback lines, and runs one `JSONResponse` through `run_request`. It also asserts the parsed body types and the converted error response. ``` # base (30aded62d4), fix reverted $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k reuse_type_adapters E AssertionError: Expected 'mock' to not have been called. Called 8 times. 1 failed, 55 deselected # this PR $ pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py -k reuse_type_adapters 1 passed, 55 deselected ``` **Existing unit tests.** All tests in `tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py` that do not launch a model pass locally (43 passed). The 13 model-backed tests (`test_embeddings`, `test_score`, ...) need a vLLM build I don't have on macOS, so they are left to the Entrypoints Unit CI step. **Equivalence.** I compared the original and patched modules side by side on 13 input lines and 4 responses. Inputs: embeddings str/list/tokens/chat, extra field, missing input, bad type, score text/queries-documents/invalid, chat, fallback valid/invalid. Responses: embedding, error, unparseable body, handler exception. All 17 results are identical. **Microbenchmark.** Apple M1 Pro, CPU only. 20k `/v1/embeddings` lines (`dimensions=128`) and a stub handler that returns an `EmbeddingResponse` as a `JSONResponse`. No model or engine is involved. The table shows the median of 3 alternating runs, with the range in brackets. | step | before | after | |---|---|---| | pass 1: `validate_batch` | 689 µs [678–718] | 26 µs [25–27] | | pass 2: `run_one_request` (parse + handler + response conversion) | 1,254 µs [1,233–1,441] | 151 µs [144–154] | | **total per line** | **1,952 µs [1,932–2,130]** | **178 µs [169–179]** | | 1.45M lines (scaled) | 47.2 min | 4.3 min | **End to end.** I have not run an end-to-end comparison on main. In our deployment on v0.31.0, which has the same per-request `TypeAdapter` code, a 1.45M-line embeddings batch spent 25.5 min just reading input (~950 lines/s). Processing was capped at 1,150–1,600 req/s, which matches the ~0.63 ms per response conversion on the event loop. With this change applied as a patch, the end-to-end batch time went from about 60 min to about 20 min.
Benchmark script (python bench_run_batch.py path/to/run_batch.py) ```python """Per-line cost of the run-batch flow: validate_batch pass + run_one_request. Usage: python bench_run_batch.py """ import asyncio import hashlib import importlib.util import io import json import random import sys import time from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.embed.protocol import ( EmbeddingResponse, EmbeddingResponseData, ) import vllm.entrypoints.launchers # noqa: F401 (parent package for relative imports) spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location( "vllm.entrypoints.launchers.rb_bench", sys.argv[1] ) rb = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec) spec.loader.exec_module(rb) N_IN, N_REQ, PROD = 20000, 5000, 1_451_852 print("module:", sys.argv[1]) base = "Recent interests: camping gear, hiking boots, outdoor clothing, travel, coffee. " lines = [ json.dumps( { "custom_id": "_" + hashlib.md5(str(i).encode()).hexdigest(), "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": { "model": "vllm", "input": (base * (1 + i % 4)) + f"#{i}", "dimensions": 128, }, }, ensure_ascii=False, ) for i in range(N_IN) ] for ln in lines[:200]: rb.BatchRequestInput.model_validate_json(ln) def report(label, per_us): print(f"{label:<34} per={per_us:8.1f}us -> {per_us * PROD / 1e6 / 60:5.1f} min") t0 = time.perf_counter() for ln in lines: rb.BatchRequestInput.model_validate_json(ln) report("parse model_validate_json", (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N_IN * 1e6) t0 = time.perf_counter() n = rb.validate_batch(io.StringIO("\n".join(lines) + "\n")) assert n == N_IN validate_per = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / N_IN * 1e6 report("pass1 validate_batch", validate_per) usage = EmbeddingResponse.model_fields["usage"].annotation(prompt_tokens=30, total_tokens=30) rnd = random.Random(0) payloads = [ EmbeddingResponse( id="embd-x", created=0, model="vllm", data=[ EmbeddingResponseData( index=0, embedding=[rnd.uniform(-0.2, 0.2) for _ in range(128)] ) ], usage=usage, ).model_dump() for _ in range(N_REQ) ] async def run_all(): it = iter(payloads) async def handler(_body): return JSONResponse(content=next(it)) registry = { "embeddings": { "url": "/v1/embeddings", "handler_getter": lambda: handler, "wrapper_fn": None, } } t0 = time.perf_counter() outs = [await rb.run_one_request(lines[i], registry) for i in range(N_REQ)] return outs, time.perf_counter() - t0 outs, el = asyncio.run(run_all()) bad = sum( 1 for o in outs if o.error is not None or not isinstance(o.response.body, EmbeddingResponse) ) run_per = el / N_REQ * 1e6 report("pass2 run_one_request (loop)", run_per) print(f" bad={bad}, event-loop cap ~{1e6 / run_per:,.0f} req/s") report("total pass1 + pass2", validate_per + run_per) ```
## Details **Root cause.** - Input side: `TypeAdapter(...)` inside `BatchRequestInput.check_type_for_url`, added in #12420. - Response side: `TypeAdapter(AllResponse | ErrorResponse)` in `run_request`, added in #28631. It also builds a new `Union` object on every call, so caching by type identity would not help. A module constant is the simplest fix. - Since #52505, each line is parsed twice: once in `validate_batch` before the engine starts, and again in `run_one_request` on the event loop. That doubles the input-side cost. **Import cost.** Building the four adapters adds about 2–3 ms at import. `vllm.entrypoints.cli.run_batch.subparser_init` imports this module for every `vllm` CLI invocation, including `vllm serve`, so the cost applies there too. It is negligible against the module's ~9 s import. **Safety.** `TypeAdapter.validate_python` does not keep per-call state, so sharing one adapter across concurrent requests is safe. vLLM never calls `model_rebuild` on these models at runtime, so a cached adapter cannot hold a stale schema. **Scope.** I checked the other per-call `TypeAdapter(...)` sites under `vllm/entrypoints`. They run only on rare paths: a dict `structural_tag` `response_format`, and the Responses API streaming error path. `sagemaker` already caches its adapters. This PR leaves them alone. **Duplicate check.** As of 2026-10-22, searching vllm-project/vllm issues and PRs for `TypeAdapter run_batch` / `run_batch TypeAdapter` returns nothing. None of the open PRs that touch `run_batch` (#51859, #57825, #59716) change this code. ---

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --root-path
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support `--root-path` on the Rust frontend, which a placeholder rejected at startup: every route is served both under the prefix and at its bare path, as with the Python frontend's FastAPI `root_path`.

## Claims

- With `--root-path /llm`, `/llm/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions` both reach the chat route, on `vllm-rs serve` and on the Python launcher path.
- API-key auth guards the prefixed paths too, and HTTP metric labels and load tracking see the bare path.
- The prefix only matches up to a path segment boundary (`/llmx/...` is not stripped), and the query string is kept.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2379 tests run: 2379 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `routes::tests::root_path_serves_routes_under_prefix_and_at_bare_paths`: with API keys and `/llm`, `/v1/models` and `/llm/v1/models` return 200, `/llm/v1/models` without a token returns 401, `/llmx/v1/models` and `/llm` return 404. It fails with the stripping disabled.
- `routes::tests::strip_root_path_keeps_query_and_segment_boundary`: snapshot of the rewritten URIs (`/llm/v1/models?limit=1` → `/v1/models?limit=1`, `/llm` → `/`, `/llmx/...` and bare paths unchanged).
- `cli::tests::root_path_reaches_config_from_serve_args_and_args_json`: the final `Config` on both launch paths.
- E2E on GB200 with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and a `vllm-rs` built from this branch: `pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_root_path.py`: 4 passed. It can join the Rust frontend CI step in a follow-up.

## Details

Python's `--root-path` sets FastAPI's `root_path` (`vllm/entrypoints/launchers/app.py`). Starlette then routes a request whose path starts with the root path as if the prefix were absent (`starlette._utils.get_route_path`), while bare paths keep working, and the API-key middleware strips the prefix before deciding whether a path is guarded (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/middleware/authenticate.py`). `test_root_path.py` pins exactly this.

- `--root-path` becomes a real `SharedRuntimeArgs` option carried into `Config::root_path` on both launch paths (an empty value means no root path, like FastAPI).
- `routes::with_root_path` wraps the finished router (including router extensions) in an outer router whose fallback service strips the prefix, then routes.

**Layering.** The consumer is HTTP routing, so the prefix is stripped in the server crate before routing; an `axum` `Router::layer` runs after routing and cannot rewrite the routed path. Every layer then sees the bare path, so API-key auth, HTTP metric labels and load tracking need no root-path awareness, matching Python's auth and route-template metric labels.

Not mirrored: FastAPI's OpenAPI `servers` entry derived from `root_path`; the Rust frontend serves no docs routes.

Not a duplicate: supersedes the inactive vllm-project/vllm#44900 (no activity since 2026-09-03), which registered every route twice through `Router::nest`; with nesting, `MatchedPath` and therefore the HTTP metric labels carry the prefix, and auth sees the prefixed path. commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Report the generate response envelope like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Report the `/inference/v1/generate` response envelope like the Python frontend: `model`, `created`, `usage` and `output_mode` on non-streaming responses, and `output_mode` on every streamed chunk. The Rust frontend omitted all four, so a client reading `usage` from a non-streaming generate response, which vllm-project/vllm#42748 added for disaggregated serving, got nothing.

## Claims

- Non-streaming responses carry `model` (the LoRA adapter name when the request resolved to one, otherwise the first served model name, as on chat and completions), `created`, `usage` (prompt, completion and total tokens, plus `prompt_tokens_details` under `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`) and `output_mode: "tokens"`. As in Python, `usage` does not depend on `stream_options`.
- Every streamed chunk, including the usage-only chunk, carries `output_mode: "tokens"`. Chunks still carry no `model` or `created`, as in Python.
- `output_mode` is always `tokens`: `text` and `derender` still return 400 on the Rust frontend.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2377 tests run: 2377 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `non_stream_raw_generate_returns_token_output_envelope` and `stream_raw_generate_returns_sse_chunks_and_usage` fail on `output_mode` without the route changes; `collect_generate_reports_cached_prompt_tokens_in_usage` fails when `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` is ignored. All pass with them.
- The first commit is a behavior-preserving extraction; its own run is green too.

## Details

Python builds the non-streaming response with `model_dump()` (`scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py` `_build_response_fields`, `protocol.py` `GenerateResponseBase`), so every field is present. `usage` was added on purpose in vllm-project/vllm#42748, and `output_mode` has been the response discriminator since vllm-project/vllm#58588 (`test_generate_stream.py` pins `"tokens"`). The old Rust comment "non-streaming raw generate responses do not include usage" mirrored Python from before #42748.

- Commit 1 moves the response-model rule, duplicated in the chat and completions `convert.rs`, into `LoraModelResolution::response_model()` without changing behavior, so generate reuses it instead of adding a third copy.
- Commit 2 adds the fields to the generate response DTOs (`routes/inference/generate/types.rs`) and fills them in `collect_generate` and the chunk stream; `usage` reuses `Usage::from_token_usage`, which the streaming path already uses. Nothing below the server crate changes.

**Differences from Python kept.** `usage.completion_tokens_details` is serialized as on the other routes today (`{"reasoning_tokens": 0}`) where Python sends `null`; vllm-project/vllm#64219 changes that on every route. Python's token chunks serialize `"usage": null` and choice-level `null`s; Rust omits them, as before.

**Merge note.** vllm-project/vllm#64219 adds a `reasoning_tokens` argument to `Usage::from_token_usage`; whichever of the two lands second passes `None` at the new `collect_generate` call site. vllm-project/vllm#64514 (`VLLM_SKIP_MODEL_NAME_Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2377 tests run: 2377 passed, 13 skipped
````) touches the same response-model lines in chat and completions `convert.rs`; whichever lands second is a one-line rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --max-log-len
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support `--max-log-len` on the Rust frontend, which a placeholder rejected at startup. It bounds the output text and token IDs that `--enable-log-outputs` logs, like the Python frontend's `RequestLogger`.

## Claims

- `--max-log-len N` is accepted on `vllm-rs serve` and on the Python launcher path.
- Complete and delta output logs on chat, completions and generate log at most the first `N` characters of text (Unicode scalar values, like Python's `str` slicing) and the first `N` token IDs.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2378 tests run: 2378 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `routes::tests::max_log_len_truncates_logged_outputs_and_token_ids`: a streamed chat request with `--max-log-len 1` and delta logging logs every delta and the complete output cut to one character and one token ID; it covers the cases of Python's `test_request_logger_log_outputs_with_truncation`, and fails with the truncation removed.
- `routes::tests::max_log_len_counts_characters`: `"中😀a"` with limits 2, 0 and 100 logs `"中😀"`, `""` and the full text, and the token IDs `[1, 2]`, `[]` and all three, like Python's slices.
- `cli::tests::frontend_args_json_passes_output_logging_into_config` also checks `max_log_len`.

## Details

Python's `RequestLogger` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py`) truncates everything it logs about a request to `max_log_len`: the prompt and prompt token IDs, the request body, and the output text and token IDs (`log_outputs`). The Rust frontend logs generated outputs for `--enable-log-outputs` since vllm-project/vllm#63769, so the flag now has a Rust consumer.

- `ApiServerOptions::log_outputs` becomes an `OutputLogConfig`: which outputs to log (the existing `OutputLogging` mode) plus `max_log_len`, built once from the CLI, with the same `logs_complete()`/`logs_deltas()` predicates.
- Its `log` method (formerly the free `output_log::log_output`, same body and comments) applies the bound. Call sites pass only the event: kind, text, token IDs and finish reason.

**Layering.** Like Python's `RequestLogger(max_log_len=...)`, the bound is fixed at construction in the one value that owns output logging, and `OutputLogConfig::log` is the only place the Rust frontend logs request content. The handlers and the chat `StreamDeltaLog` hold that value instead of threading `max_log_len` next to it. The Rust frontend does not log prompts or request bodies yet, so those parts of Python's truncation have nothing to apply to; whichever change adds prompt logging should apply the same bound.

**Deviation.** Python accepts a negative `--max-log-len` and slices from the end (`s[:-3]`); the Rust frontend takes a non-negative integer and rejects a negative value at startup.

Not a duplicate: supersedes vllm-project/vllm#57527, closed on 2026-10-23 after going inactive; it predates Rust output logging and only bounded a new DEBUG prompt-token-ID log line. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `echo` and `logprobs`, streamed `/v1/completions` on the Rust frontend now requests and reports the prompt logprobs with the echoed prompt, like the Python frontend.

## Claims

- A streamed `echo` + `logprobs` request asks the engine for prompt logprobs, and the echoed prompt chunk carries `logprobs` for the prompt tokens from text offset 0 (the first prompt token with `null` logprob and top logprobs).
- The generated tokens' `text_offset` continues after the reported prompt tokens, as in Python, instead of after the prompt's character count.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2377 tests run: 2377 passed, 13 skipped
```

New route test `completions_echo_stream_reports_prompt_logprobs`: the mock engine checks that the request carries `prompt_logprobs=1` and returns prompt logprobs with the first output. The stream reports `hello` with tokens `h e l l o`, logprobs `[null, -0.3, -0.4, -0.45, -0.5]`, first top logprobs `null`, offsets `0..4`, then `h` at offset 5 and `i` at offset 6. A `return_tokens_as_token_ids` case makes the reported prompt tokens (`token_id:NNN`, 60 characters) longer than the prompt text, so the generated offsets are 60 and 72. It fails on `main` (no `prompt_logprobs` on the engine request), with only the lowering change (no `logprobs` on the prompt chunk), and with the old text-length offset.

## Details

Python's `CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params` falls back to `logprobs` for `prompt_logprobs` when `echo` is set, and `completion_stream_generator` reports them with the echoed prompt (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py`). Rust requested prompt logprobs only for non-streaming or prompt-only (`max_tokens=0`) echo, so a streamed echo returned the prompt chunk without `logprobs`.

- `completions/convert.rs`: request prompt logprobs for every `echo` with `logprobs`, like Python. An explicit `prompt_logprobs` still wins, and an explicit one with `stream` is still rejected by validation, as in Python.
- `completion_chunk_stream`: attach the prompt logprobs to the echoed prompt chunk through the helper that prompt-only echo already used (renamed `prompt_only_logprobs_to_openai` → `echoed_prompt_logprobs_to_openai`, since it now serves every echo), and advance the next text offset by the reported prompt tokens.

**Layering.** The sampling-param lowering and the SSE chunk shape are both completions-protocol behavior owned by the completions route in `vllm-server`; the text layer already decodes prompt logprobs into the `Start` event.

**Remaining difference.** Rust streams the echoed prompt as its own chunk before the first generated chunk, while Python sends the prompt and the first generated text in one chunk. The concatenated `text` and `logprobs` across chunks are identical.

Not a duplicate: first-time contributor PRs vllm-project/vllm#62684 (echo with `return_token_ids`) and vllm-project/vllm#63926 (logprob token strings) touch the same files but not this behavior; this diff stays in the echo `Start` branch and the lowering line. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support return_weight_versions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support `return_weight_versions` on the Rust frontend's `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`, which a placeholder (vllm-project/vllm#62434) rejected with 400. Python returns the per-choice weight-version spans since vllm-project/vllm#61347.

## Claims

- With `return_weight_versions: true`, every finished chat and completions choice carries `weight_versions`, a list of `{version, start, end}` spans over output-token indexes, cut at the stop-string truncated output as Python does. Streaming puts the spans on the final chunk of each choice only.
- Without the option, responses are unchanged. `/inference/v1/generate` keeps returning spans on its final chunk only.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2377 tests run: 2377 passed, 13 skipped
```

New tests:

- `vllm-text` `stream_stop_string_cuts_weight_version_spans_at_truncated_count`: a stop string ending inside a merged output that spans two more versions; the spans are cut at the truncated count (fails without the cut).
- `vllm-server` `openai_return_weight_versions_reports_spans_on_final_choice`: chat and completions × stream and non-stream × opt-in on and off, through the mock engine with a `v1` → `v2` weight update; spans only on the final choice when opted in (fails with the chat choice wiring reverted).
- `vllm-server` `generate_chunk_stream_returns_weight_versions_on_final_chunk_only` (fails without the final-chunk filter).
- The `vllm-llm` `stream_interval` test now expects cumulative spans on every output.

## Details

Python computes the spans in `OutputProcessor` over the stop-string truncated output (`_weight_version_spans`, `vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py`). The data already reached Rust: `vllm-llm` tracks the engine's per-step `weight_version` label and builds the spans for `/inference/v1/generate`. The chat and completions paths dropped them.

- **`vllm-llm`**: `GenerateOutput.weight_versions` is now set on every output, as the spans over the output so far, instead of on terminal outputs only. The text layer can finish a request locally after matching a stop string, on an output the engine did not mark terminal, and then needs the spans to cut them, the way Python cuts them at its truncated token count.
- **`vllm-text`**: on the terminal output, the decoder cuts the spans at the stop-string truncated `output_token_count` (drops spans that start past it, clamps the last end) and carries them on `Finished` and `CollectedTextOutput`, next to `sampling_mask`.
- **`vllm-chat`**: the spans go through `AssistantEvent::Done`, `ChatEvent::Done` and `CollectedAssistantMessage`, like `kv_transfer_params`.
- **`vllm-server`**: the placeholder checks are removed; `ResponseOptions.return_weight_versions` gates the field on the non-streaming choice and the final streamed chunk. Completions choices gain the `weight_versions` field (`null` when unset on the non-streaming response, like Python).

**Layering.** `vllm-llm` owns the spans because it sees the per-step engine labels, including steps merged by `stream_interval`; `vllm-text` owns the cut because it owns stop-string truncation of tokens, logprobs and sampling masks. The server only decides per request whether to show them. The cost is one small `Vec` (normally one span) per output instead of per request; a per-output label instead of cumulative spans would lose exactness when outputs merge across a weight update.

**Deviations.** On streaming chunks the field is omitted when unset, as Rust does for `token_ids`, where Python sends an explicit `null` on the final chunk. Prompt-only echo (`echo` with `max_tokens: 0`) reports the span of its one internal token, as Python does.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds `return_weight_versions` to the Rust frontend. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export UMBP connector transfer metrics like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Export the UMBP store connector's `vllm:umbp_transfer_*` counters from the Rust frontend. vllm-project/vllm#61793 registered `UMBPStoreConnector` in the connector factory, so deployments can now produce these stats, but the Rust frontend decodes the payload into an unknown-connector map and drops it.

## Claims

- `vllm:umbp_transfer_submitted_total`, `vllm:umbp_transfer_completed_total`, `vllm:umbp_transfer_failed_total` and `vllm:umbp_transfer_bytes_total` are exported with Python's names, help text and labels (`model_name`, `engine`, `operation`), for a bare UMBP connector and for a `UMBPStoreConnector` child of a `MultiConnector`.
- As in Python, an operation's series appears the first time the connector reports it; the counters add up across stats intervals.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2377 tests run: 2377 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `metrics::tests::umbp_stats_are_recorded_into_umbp_transfer_metrics`: no series before the first report; a bare payload in Python's shape, recorded twice, renders all eight series with summed counters.
- `protocol::stats::tests::kv_connector_stats_ignore_unknown_fields`: a bare UMBP payload with an extra counter decodes as UMBP stats, and a MultiConnector map with NIXL, Mooncake and UMBP children keeps all three.
- `tests::client::python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding_and_record_nixl_metrics`: the Python fixture script now encodes a UMBP payload with msgspec, bare and as a MultiConnector child; Rust decodes both and records the child into `vllm:umbp_transfer_bytes_total`.
- Red-green: with the UMBP variant tried after `Multi`, the decode and fixture tests fail; with the recorder arm turned into a no-op, the metrics test fails.
- Not run against a live ROCm/MORI server.

## Details

Python's `UMBPStoreConnectorStats` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/umbp/stats.py`, vllm-project/vllm#61791) sends `{operation: {"submitted", "completed", "failed", "num_bytes"}}` with operations `load` and `store`, and `UMBPStorePromMetrics` exports the four counters. In Rust, `KvConnectorStats` is an untagged enum tried in order; a UMBP payload failed every typed variant and landed in `Multi`, where every key went to the opaque `other` map.

- `vllm-engine-core-client` `protocol/stats.rs`: `UmbpStats` (a closed `UmbpOperation` enum to per-operation counts), `KvConnectorStats::Umbp` ahead of `Multi`, and `MultiConnectorStats::umbp` under `UMBPStoreConnector`.
- `vllm-metrics` `scheduler.rs`: the four counter families.
- `vllm-engine-core-client` `metrics.rs`: `record_umbp_stats`, for both payload shapes.

**Layering.** `SchedulerStatsRecorder` in `vllm-engine-core-client` already owns decoding and recording connector stats for NIXL and Mooncake, so the UMBP decode and recorder sit beside them, and the families sit in `vllm-metrics` with every other Prometheus family. This follows the Mooncake store precedent, including lazily created per-operation series.

**Relation to vllm-project/vllm#58563** (connector-described metrics, open): it exports metrics for connectors that ship a descriptor and keeps the dedicated NIXL and Mooncake paths; it does not touch UMBP. If UMBP later adopts a descriptor, this dedicated path can go.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches UMBP metrics in the Rust frontend (searched open PRs for "UMBP metrics" and "umbp_transfer"). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Fix bad_words handling in /v1/completions
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make `bad_words` take effect on the Rust frontend's `/v1/completions`. Taking over this PR from @reidliu41: the original commit is kept as is, `main` is merged in (one mechanical conflict), and a route-level test is added on top. The original description is kept below.

## Claims

- `/v1/completions` forwards `bad_words` to sampling like `/v1/chat/completions` and the Python frontend, instead of silently dropping it.
- A route test pins that the scripted engine receives `_bad_words_token_ids` for `bad_words` on both chat and completions.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root on this branch:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2403 tests run: 2403 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `routes::tests::openai_bad_words_reach_engine_core_as_token_ids` sends `"bad_words": ["blocked"]` to both routes and checks the engine request. With the forwarding reverted, the completions case reaches the engine without bad-word token IDs and fails.
- `prepare_completion_request_maps_sampling_fields` (from the original commit) checks the field on the lowered text request; it fails without the change too.

## Details

Python's `CompletionRequest` declares `bad_words: list[str] = []` and passes it to `SamplingParams` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py`), like chat. The Rust completions DTO did not declare it, so the value landed in the flattened `other` map, and request conversion lowered `bad_words: None`: the request succeeded and the words were not banned. Declaring the field and passing it through reuses the existing text-layer tokenization (`vllm-text` `lower_sampling_params`, shared with chat and generate), so no other change is needed.

Changes on top of the original commit:

- Merge of `main`: `CompletionRequest` lowering gained `bad_words_token_ids` and `logprob_token_ids` since this branch was cut; the conflict keeps both next to `bad_words: request.bad_words`.
- The route test above, which observes the engine request rather than the intermediate text request, so a later routing or lowering regression on either route is caught.

Not a duplicate: this is the existing PR for the item, taken over after it went inactive (last activity 2026-10-07). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare the takeover; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

<details>
<summary>Original description by @reidliu41</summary>

## Purpose

  The Rust `/v1/completions` request type did not declare `bad_words`. The field was captured by the flattened extra-fields map, while request conversion always set `SamplingParams.bad_words` to `None`.

  As a result, requests containing `bad_words` succeeded, but the requested filtering was silently not applied.

  Declare `bad_words` as a typed completion request field and forward it into `SamplingParams`. This connects `/v1/completions` to the existing bad-word tokenization and filtering pipeline. It also ensures invalid `bad_words` element types return a request error instead of being silently accepted.

## Test Plan

```
  cargo nextest run -p vllm-server prepare_completion_request_maps_sampling_fields
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Add size-gated PDL to silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds programmatic dependent launch (PDL) to the fused SiLU-mul + NVFP4 quant kernel (`silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`)
- `griddepcontrol.wait` + `launch_dependents` at kernel start (sm90+).
- The placement is quite aggressive, hence there is a gate `M * N/16 <= SMs * 4096` (there is regression for large M)

## Claims

- **−4.7 % (C=1), −4.1 % (C=4), −4.6 % (C=16)** TPOT, mean of 3 alternating rounds on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 TP1 (8k in / 1k out); C=64 in noise. TTFT neutral (gate off at prefill chunks).
- **Bitwise identical** outputs and scale bytes; PDL changes no math.

## Validation

### Chain microbenchmark (primary)

- Real production chain per layer — `scaled_fp4_quant(x)` → gate_up `mm_fp4` → `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` → down `mm_fp4` (FlashInfer CuTe-DSL calls as deployed)
- captured in one CUDA graph over 6 distinct layers (~1.2 GB of weights, HBM-cold). 20 graph replays timed with CUDA events; 5 fresh processes per arm, arms interleaved and shuffled per round.
- A = PR (gated), B = base, B2 = base again (noise floor), C = gate removed (measurement only).

**27B TP1, N = 17408 (gate at M = 557):**

| M | A | B | B2 | C | A−B | B−B2 | C−B |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 32.39 | 33.72 | 33.71 | 32.34 | **−1.33** | +0.01 | −1.38 |
| 8 | 32.76 | 34.03 | 34.04 | 32.73 | −1.27 | −0.01 | −1.30 |
| 16 | 33.16 | 34.43 | 34.45 | 33.42 | −1.26 | −0.02 | −1.01 |
| 32 | 35.05 | 35.96 | 35.99 | 35.07 | −0.91 | −0.03 | −0.89 |
| 64 | 37.21 | 37.52 | 37.60 | 36.78 | −0.31 | −0.08 | −0.74 |
| 128 | 40.50 | 39.86 | 39.85 | 40.29 | +0.64 | +0.01 | +0.43 |
| 256 | 47.82 | 48.74 | 48.75 | 47.78 | −0.92 | −0.02 | −0.96 |
| 512 | 70.11 | 70.22 | 70.19 | 70.19 | −0.12 | +0.04 | −0.03 |
| 544 | 97.27 | 97.54 | 97.52 | 97.20 | −0.27 | +0.02 | −0.34 |
| 576 (off) | 97.23 | 97.99 | 97.93 | 97.86 | −0.77 | +0.06 | −0.13 |
| 768 (off) | 103.40 | 103.80 | 103.86 | 104.40 | −0.40 | −0.06 | **+0.60** |
| 1152 (off) | 136.90 | 137.21 | 137.53 | 139.16 | −0.31 | −0.33 | **+1.95** |
| 2048 (off) | 206.52 | 206.82 | 206.82 | 210.18 | −0.31 | 0.00 | **+3.35** |
| 4096 (off) | 852.17 | 851.46 | 851.70 | 857.83 | +0.71 | −0.25 | **+6.37** |
| 8192 (off) | 1645.10 | 1640.99 | 1642.44 | 1663.03 | +4.11 | −1.46 | **+22.04** |

### E2E (vllm serve + vllm bench serve, random dataset)

Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, TP1, 1× B300, default CUDA graphs, `--language-model-only`, `vllm bench serve` random dataset with `--ignore-eos`. Median TPOT (ms), mean of 3 rounds, A B A B on one GPU plus a base-only run; base same-arm spread ±0.4 % at C=1, ±2.0 % at C=64 (PR spread at C=1: ±0.01 %).

| Workload (8k/1k) | base → PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|
| C=1 | 5.424 → 5.169 | −4.7 % |
| C=4 | 6.143 → 5.894 | −4.1 % |
| C=16 | 8.546 → 8.154 | −4.6 % |
| C=64 | 16.671 → 16.533 | −0.8 % (in noise) |

The effect exceeds the MLP-chain prediction (−1.33 µs × 64 layers ≈ −1.6 %): all four linears per layer (qkv, o, gate_up, down) are PDL-launched `mm_fp4`s, so the overlap propagates along the whole per-layer chain. TTFT neutral: ~196 (base) vs ~193 ms (PR) at C=1 — the 8k prefill chunks sit off-gate.

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`: 20/20 pass (B300), including #63382's scale-padding cases.
- Bitwise: FP4 data + all scale bytes identical PR vs base on 8 shapes (M = 1, 3, 64, 555, 558, 2048 at I = 17408 — straddling the gate at 557 — and M = 1, 256 at I = 512), md5 of raw bytes.

commits.pr_title: [Compile] Make the compile cache device-neutral with compile_on_one_rank
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make the torch.compile cache device-neutral, so a cache built on one GPU can be reused on another. Since #45026 a worker's local rank no longer implies its device, so a cache built with `--device-ids 0` and reused with `--device-ids 1` crashes on startup. This enables torch 2.14's `compile_on_one_rank` mode via a new `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` (default on for torch >= 2.14 on CUDA/ROCm and XPU).

## Claims

- Fixes `CUDA driver error: invalid argument` during the first warm-up forward when a compile cache built on one device is reused on another (`--device-ids`).
- The cache is reused across device indices with no recompile.
- `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` is part of the compile cache key: caches built with the mode off are never loaded with it on, and vice versa.
- No throughput or output change (TP=1 and TP=2, greedy outputs identical).

## Validation

All runs: Qwen3-0.6B, 2x H100, torch 2.14.0, `vllm serve --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5`, one fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` shared by the runs of each table.

**Reproducer.** Run A builds the cache, then B and C reuse it:

| Run | Device in-process | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| A `--device-ids 0` | cuda:0 | Up, compiles, writes the cache | Up, compiles, writes the cache |
| B `--device-ids 1` | cuda:1 | **Crash**: loads A's AOT cache, `CUDA driver error: invalid argument` | **Up**: loads A's AOT cache, no recompile |
| C `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` (control) | cuda:0 | Up | Up |

C runs on the same physical GPU as B and reuses the same cache, but in-process it is `cuda:0`, so the device index alone decides the failure.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --device-ids 0 --port 8000   # A: wait until healthy, then stop
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --device-ids 1 --port 8000   # B: crashes before this PR
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8000  # C: control
```
</details>

**What changes in the cached code.** Counts over the generated Inductor modules in the cache:

| | Literal device index (`_DeviceGuard(0)`, `get_raw_stream(0)`, `DeviceProperties(..., index=0`) | Runtime expression (`torch.cuda.current_device()`, `index=None`) |
|---|---|---|
| Mode off | 76 | 0 |
| Mode on | 0 | 62 |

**Cache-key isolation.** Starting with `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK=0` on a cache root built with the mode on recompiles instead of loading it.

**TP=2.** Cold and warm start with the mode on and off: warm starts load both ranks' caches with no recompile, and there are no CUDA errors.

**Outputs.** Greedy completions (32 tokens, 3 prompts) are identical with the mode on and off, at TP=1 and TP=2.

**Throughput.** `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 300 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 0`, one run per cell:

| | Output tok/s (off → on) | Mean TPOT ms (off → on) | Mean TTFT ms (off → on) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP=1 | 12,283 → 12,459 | 3.88 → 3.80 | 134.6 → 137.4 |
| TP=2 | 13,372 → 13,653 | 3.36 → 3.34 | 149.3 → 140.5 |

The differences are within run-to-run variation.

**Tests.** `tests/compile/test_compile_on_one_rank.py`: the default and its gates, the flag being a compile cache factor that changes the hash, `env_override` applying it to torch, and (on CUDA) that Inductor's generated code bakes in the device index with the mode off and resolves it at run time with it on. It runs in the existing `find compile/ -maxdepth 1 -name 'test_*.py'` Buildkite step.

## Details

**Root cause.** The AOT compile cache lives under `torch_aot_compile/<hash>/rank_{rank}_{dp_rank}`, where the hash covers the vLLM config and env factors. Neither includes the device. That was safe while rank r always ran on `cuda:r`. Since #45026, `--device-ids` maps logical ranks to physical devices without narrowing `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, so a rank can run on any device index. Inductor bakes the compile-time device in two places:

1. **The generated wrapper code:** `torch.cuda._DeviceGuard(0)`, `torch.cuda.set_device(0)`, `get_raw_stream(0)`.
2. **Each Triton kernel's load device:** statically launched kernels are loaded into the device recorded at compile time.

Reusing the cache on `cuda:1` launches kernels against `cuda:0`'s stream (`invalid argument`). In an experiment on torch 2.13, rewriting only the wrapper code still failed (`invalid resource handle`), because the kernels are loaded into `cuda:0`'s context. Both have to be device-relative.

**Fix.** torch 2.14's `torch.compiler.config.compile_on_one_rank` makes Inductor emit `torch.cuda.current_device()` in the wrapper and compile kernels with `DeviceProperties(index=None)`. That covers both places, so no Inductor patching is needed in vLLM. Torch also includes the mode in Inductor's own cache key. vLLM's AOT cache key needs it as well, which a registered vLLM env var provides through `envs.compile_factors()`. `env_override` sets torch's config from `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` in every vLLM process, so an outside `TORCH_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` cannot make the compiled code disagree with the cache key.

**Relation to #38962 / #53312.** #38962 fixed the same crash by adding the device index to the cache path; it was reverted in #53304 for a CPU regression, and #53312 re-lands it. That approach stops the crash but gives each device index its own cache, so replicas on different GPUs recompile instead of sharing one. This PR keeps a single cache that works on any device index, and its default is off on CPU. The two can coexist; with this PR, device-keyed paths are no longer needed for correctness.

**Limitations.**
- On torch < 2.14 the mode does not exist, so the default stays off and the bug remains. Fixing it there would need patches to Inductor's codegen and its static Triton launcher.
- The default is off on platforms other than CUDA/ROCm and XPU, because Inductor raises for backends without `current_device_idx_expr()`.
- Existing caches recompile once after upgrading, because the cache key changes.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support hybrid and external DP LB in `vllm-rs serve`
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support hybrid and external data parallel load balancing in standalone `vllm-rs serve`, with the same flags as `vllm serve`: one Rust frontend per node or per DP rank, each serving only its own ranks.

Top of a stack: vllm-project/vllm#64449 → vllm-project/vllm#64450 → this PR.

## Claims

- `vllm-rs serve` accepts `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`, `--data-parallel-external-lb`, `--data-parallel-rank` (or `VLLM_DP_RANK`), and `--data-parallel-start-rank` outside `--headless`. Until now the first three were rejected as unsupported.
- A hybrid-LB frontend serves its node's ranks, and an external-LB frontend serves its single rank. `X-data-parallel-rank` takes the global rank.
- For MoE models, the rank-0 frontend runs the DP coordinator and the other frontends follow its waves.

## Validation

GB200 node, DP 4 with one GPU per rank, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 2048`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.3`:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| MoE (`TitanML/tiny-mixtral`), internal LB, two launchers: rank 0 plus `--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 2` | Requests pinned to ranks 0–3 and an unpinned request return 200; 32/32 concurrent requests succeed |
| MoE, hybrid LB: frontend 8100 with ranks 0–1 (`--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`), frontend 8101 with ranks 2–3 (`--data-parallel-start-rank 2`) | Own ranks and unpinned requests return 200 on both; rank 0 pinned on 8101 returns 400; bursts of 32 sent to 8101 only, then 8100 only, then 8101 again all return 200 |
| MoE, external LB: four frontends with `--data-parallel-rank 0..3` | Each returns 200; 32 concurrent requests to rank 3's frontend only all return 200, which needs the other ranks' engines to follow its waves |
| Dense (`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`), hybrid LB: same layout as the MoE hybrid run | Own ranks and unpinned requests return 200 on both frontends, with the same greedy output on every rank; bursts of 32 sent to 8100 only and to 8101 only all return 200 |

All rows are from the current heads of this stack.

<details>
<summary>Hybrid LB commands</summary>

```bash
COMMON="--data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 2 --data-parallel-address 127.0.0.1 \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 29652 --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --enforce-eager"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm-rs serve TitanML/tiny-mixtral $COMMON --data-parallel-hybrid-lb --port 8100
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vllm-rs serve TitanML/tiny-mixtral $COMMON --data-parallel-start-rank 2 --port 8101
```

External LB: one process per rank `r` with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$r vllm-rs serve TitanML/tiny-mixtral --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-rank $r --data-parallel-address 127.0.0.1 --data-parallel-rpc-port 29653 --port $((8100 + r)) ...`.

</details>

Tests (these use inline `expect-test` snapshots):

- `resolve_follows_vllm_serve_dp_lb_modes` (in `vllm-managed-engine`, next to the resolution rules in the new `data_parallel` module): a table of flag combinations and the resulting ranks or error.
- `serve_rank_zero_frontend_hosts_the_coordinator_for_its_single_rank`: an external-LB rank-0 frontend with one local rank still runs the coordinator.
- `serve_hybrid_lb_frontend_connects_only_its_ranks`: a rank-2 frontend's client config and the Python engine command it launches.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` in `rust/`: 2385 passed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The Python change (a hidden `vllm serve` flag) is not covered by Python CI; the GPU runs above exercise it.

## Details

Flag resolution follows `vllm serve`'s `EngineArgs.create_engine_config`:

- A start rank outside `--headless` implies hybrid LB, and hybrid LB with every rank on the node is internal LB.
- `--data-parallel-rank` selects external LB with one local rank.
- Without `--data-parallel-size-local`, the start rank is ignored.
- Rejected: hybrid together with external LB, hybrid LB with `--headless`, a rank together with a start rank, external LB without a rank or with a local size other than 1, hybrid LB without a local size, and a rank range beyond the DP size.

Launch: the rank-0 frontend binds the shared handshake on `--data-parallel-address:--data-parallel-rpc-port`, as before. Any other frontend binds a local IPC handshake and starts its managed Python engines as a headless node with its start rank and local size, passing that endpoint as the new hidden `--headless-client-handshake-address`. `run_headless` hands it to `CoreEngineProcManager` as `client_handshake_address` with `local_client=True`, so the engines handshake with rank 0 for the coordinator and rendezvous and with their own frontend for input/output. The README gains a section on these modes.

Differences from `vllm serve`:

- `--data-parallel-rpc-port` has no default in hybrid and external LB, because every node must agree on it.
- Ranks are not inferred from `--nnodes`/`--node-rank`.
- Dense models are not rejected for external LB. `vllm serve` rejects them and points to independent instances instead.

A pre-existing issue, also present with Python-supervised hybrid LB on `main`: a request pinned to a rank the frontend does not own returns 400, but the body says only `engine-core error`. The detailed message ("rank 0 is not connected to this frontend; connected ranks: [2, 3]") is lost when the error is wrapped.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Let the handshake owner serve a range of DP ranks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Let the Rust handshake owner (managed `vllm-rs serve`) serve a range of the data parallel ranks, so several Rust frontends can split one DP deployment. The change is limited to `vllm-engine-core-client`: there is no CLI, Python, or INIT wire change, and nothing sets a nonzero start rank until vllm-project/vllm#64451 adds the `vllm-rs serve` flags.

Stack: vllm-project/vllm#64449 → this PR → vllm-project/vllm#64451.

## Claims

- `TransportMode::HandshakeOwner` takes `engine_start_index` and a deployment-wide `data_parallel_size` next to `engine_count`, like `TransportMode::Bootstrapped`. Existing callers keep internal LB by passing start rank 0 and their engine count as the DP size, with unchanged behavior.
- The frontend whose range starts at rank 0 handshakes with every rank but registers only its own engines. Other frontends handshake only with their own engines and find the coordinator through READY `dp_stats_address`.
- The in-process coordinator publishes its wave state on a frontend-facing XPUB (`frontend_stats_publish_address`), in the tuple format of Python's coordinator, so the frontends of other ranks stamp requests with the current wave.
- A misconfigured multi-frontend deployment fails at startup with a clear error instead of hanging: an engine of an unexpected rank, a remote rank's engine that joins headless, or, under coordinated DP, engines that report different `parallel_config_hash`.

## Validation

- `hybrid_lb_frontends_split_ranks_and_follow_rank_zero_coordinator`: two frontends (ranks 0 and 1) and a mock engine that handshakes with both, as a Python engine on a hybrid-LB node does. Each frontend connects only to its own engine, and the rank-1 frontend stamps requests with the wave that rank 0's coordinator advanced to. Fails without the registration filtering.
- `coordinator_publishes_wave_state_to_frontend_subscribers`: a subscriber receives the current state on subscribe and each new state after wave transitions, checked byte for byte against the msgpack tuple.
- `partitioned_handshake_rejects_unexpected_ranks_and_headless_remote_engines` and `handshake_checks_parallel_config_hashes_only_for_coordinated_dp` (dense ranks with different hashes still connect).
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` in `rust/`: 2382 passed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- End to end through vllm-project/vllm#64451 on GB200 with a MoE model: hybrid and external DP LB, including a burst sent to one frontend only, which completes while the other ranks' engines follow its waves. See vllm-project/vllm#64451 for the results.

## Details

Python's `vllm serve` supports hybrid DP LB (`--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`, one frontend per node) and external DP LB (`--data-parallel-rank`, one frontend per rank). Standalone `vllm-rs serve` supports only internal DP LB, because its handshake owner assumes it owns every engine. This PR adds the transport and coordinator side; vllm-project/vllm#64451 adds the CLI.

Roles, as in Python's `launch_core_engines`:

- The frontend whose range starts at rank 0 binds the shared handshake and handshakes with all `data_parallel_size` engines, so engines of other ranks fetch the coordinator addresses and the DP rendezvous there. Those engines take their input/output addresses from their own frontend, so only rank 0's own engines register with it. For MoE it runs the in-process coordinator, which `server/src/config.rs` now enables only for this frontend.
- Other frontends handshake only with their own engines, on a local endpoint, and subscribe to rank 0's coordinator publish address from READY `dp_stats_address`.
- An engine on another node handshakes with rank 0 first and then with its own frontend, through Python's existing `client_handshake_address` path; vllm-project/vllm#64451 passes that address to the managed engines.

Coordinator publish: the in-process coordinator tracks no request counts, so it publishes Python's wave-only update `(None, wave, engines_running)` after every wave transition and to each new subscriber (zmq.rs XPUB registers a subscription only when `recv()` yields it). A separate task woken by `Notify` sends the latest state, so a slow subscriber cannot block wave control toward the engines. The socket is bound whenever the coordinator runs, as in Python, although only hybrid and external LB have subscribers.

Startup checks:

- The rank-range and remote-headless checks run only when a frontend serves a subset of the ranks, which leaves internal LB as on `main`. Python also applies both to internal LB (there, remote engines must be headless); that is left for a follow-up.
- Python compares each engine's `parallel_config_hash` with the frontend's own `ParallelConfig`. The Rust frontend has no `ParallelConfig`, so it requires all engines to agree. Like Python, it checks only under coordinated DP, whose ranks share collectives.

The first two commits are a helper rename and a mechanical split of the mock engine handshake into steps. The new tests account for about 530 of the added lines, including mock-engine support for the two-handshake engine; the rest is about 340 lines of non-test code.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Send the DP rendezvous in coordinated-DP INIT
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix managed `vllm-rs serve` hanging at startup when a MoE model's data parallel engines come from more than one launcher, as in multi-node internal DP LB: the Rust handshake owner now sends the DP rendezvous in INIT, as the Python frontend does.

Bottom of a stack: this PR → vllm-project/vllm#64450 (handshake owner serves a range of DP ranks) → vllm-project/vllm#64451 (hybrid and external DP LB in `vllm-rs serve`). It fixes a bug on `main` on its own.

## Claims

- Internal DP LB with a MoE model and engines from several launchers (rank 0 on `vllm-rs serve`, other nodes on `vllm-rs serve --headless --data-parallel-start-rank ...`) starts and serves. On `main` it hangs in the gloo rendezvous.
- INIT `parallel_config` is typed: `HandshakeParallelConfig` carries an optional `DataParallelRendezvous`, encoded as its four fields or as `{}`.
- Dense models and single-launcher deployments are unchanged: they still receive `{}`.

## Validation

Reproducer on one GB200 node: `TitanML/tiny-mixtral`, DP 4 with one GPU per rank, two launchers with two local ranks each.

| Build | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | Never healthy within 420 s; the rank 0/1 engines wait in `stateless_init_dp_group` → gloo `connectFullMesh` |
| this PR | Healthy; requests pinned to ranks 0–3 and an unpinned request return 200; 32/32 concurrent requests succeed |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
COMMON="--data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 2 --data-parallel-address 127.0.0.1 \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 29660 --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --enforce-eager"
# Launcher A: frontend and ranks 0-1
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm-rs serve TitanML/tiny-mixtral $COMMON --port 8100
# Launcher B: ranks 2-3
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 vllm-rs serve TitanML/tiny-mixtral $COMMON --headless --data-parallel-start-rank 2
# Requests
for r in 0 1 2 3; do
  curl -s localhost:8100/v1/completions -H "X-data-parallel-rank: $r" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "TitanML/tiny-mixtral", "prompt": "Hello, my name is", "max_tokens": 8}'
done
```

</details>

The `main` row was measured on an earlier revision of this stack against the same base; the row for this PR is from its current head.

Tests:

- `coordinator_handshake_includes_engine_control_addresses` now runs two engines under the in-process coordinator and checks that both receive the same rendezvous: the handshake host and five distinct ports.
- `handshake_parallel_config_encodes_rendezvous_fields_or_empty_map` snapshots the msgpack encoding: the four field names, including `_data_parallel_master_port_list`, or `{}` when no rendezvous is sent.
- `multi_engine_client_shares_transport_and_routes_by_inflight_count` checks that DP without the coordinator still sends `{}`.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` in `rust/`: 2378 passed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Details

Root cause: MoE DP ranks form cross-rank torch process groups (the engine-level stateless DP group and the workers' DP world group) at `data_parallel_master_ip` and the ports in `ParallelConfig`. Each launcher's `ParallelConfig` draws its own free ports, so the ranks only agree when the handshake owner overwrites them through INIT `parallel_config`. The Python frontend does this for coordinated DP; the Rust handshake owner always sent `{}`. That works while one launcher spawns every engine. With a second launcher (another node, or a second `vllm-rs serve --headless` on the same node), each side dials its own ports and the rendezvous never completes.

Fix: when the in-process coordinator runs (coordinated DP: MoE with DP > 1), the handshake owner binds five ephemeral ports on the handshake host, which is `--data-parallel-address` and the host the engines already dial, releases them, and sends `data_parallel_master_ip`, `data_parallel_master_port`, `_data_parallel_master_port_list`, and `data_parallel_size` to every engine. Port allocation lives in a new private module, `transport/dp_rendezvous.rs`.

Differences from the Python frontend:

- `_coord_store_port` is not sent. The Rust frontend hosts no coordination TCPStore, so engines take the pre-allocated ports, as in Python without a store. Like Python's fallback, a port released before use can in principle be taken by another process in between.
- `VLLM_PORT` does not constrain these ports, consistent with the Rust frontend's other sockets (ZMQ input/output, coordinator), which all bind ephemeral ports.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Retry incomplete HTTP response bodies
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Retry HTTP downloads when the response body is interrupted. These failures currently bypass the existing retry logic, even when attempts remain.

## Claims

- Retry requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError and aiohttp.ClientPayloadError.
- Preserve the existing attempt limit and backoff, while continuing to enforce download size limits.

## Validation

Added four parameterized cases covering sync and async downloads, successful recovery, and retry exhaustion. All four fail before the fix and pass afterward.

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_connections.py -q
13 passed

pre-commit run --files vllm/connections.py tests/test_connections.py
Passed

The test file is already included in the Buildkite CPU misc job.

Also validated /v1/chat/completions/render using the LLaVA 1.5 preprocessing configuration, the same explicit chat template on both revisions, and a local HTTP image server. The attempt limit was set to 2.

| Image download | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Completes normally | HTTP 200, 1 attempt | HTTP 200, 1 attempt |
| First response is interrupted | HTTP 500, 1 attempt | HTTP 200, 2 attempts |
| Every response is interrupted | HTTP 500, 1 attempt | HTTP 500, 2 attempts |

After recovery, the rendered prompt token IDs exactly match the successful control request.

This validates HTTP preprocessing; GPU inference and upstream CI were not run.

## Details

Body-read failures use different exception classes from connection failures, so _is_retryable does not currently recognize them. This change adds those classes to the existing retry classification.

These exceptions can also represent malformed responses. Such responses may be retried, but still fail once the configured attempt limit is reached.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Bump FlashMLA to pass int64 positions to MegaAttn
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MegaAttn casts the RoPE positions from int64 to int32 in every layer because the FlashMLA fused norm + RoPE + attn + RoPE + cast kernels took int32. In a full CUDA graph each cast is a separate kernel: 40 per target forward on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. FlashMLA [d1a1c92](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/commit/d1a1c92eff2cf558ddf49293828cd2bd21ca48c4) (vllm-project/FlashMLA#38) now takes int64 positions directly and rejects int32, so this PR bumps FlashMLA and drops the cast.

## Changes

- Bump FlashMLA `e2afa5f` -> `d1a1c92`. The only change in between is #38.
- Pass `positions` straight to `fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_{decode,fwd}` in `flash_mla_mega_attn.py`.
- Same change in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`, which would otherwise fail the new dtype check.

## Validation

Earlier revisions of this PR shared one int32 cast across layers within a forward context. These numbers come from that version, with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8 x GB300 across two nodes, DP8 x TP1 + EP, 64 requests/rank, 131,072 input tokens, 2,048 output tokens, DSpark with 5 draft tokens and full decode CUDA graphs:

| Target forward | Before | Shared cast |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU time, median (ms) | 17.903 | 17.834 |
| GPU time, p10 / p90 (ms) | 17.847 / 17.996 | 17.793 / 17.941 |
| Kernels in the captured forward | 766 | 727 |

This revision removes all 40 casts, one more than the shared-cast version, and moves the conversion into the kernel. It has not been re-timed or rebuilt against the new FlashMLA yet.

```bash
pre-commit run --files cmake/external_projects/flashmla.cmake benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py
```

Pre-commit passed. No accuracy evaluation was run. RoPE math is unchanged, and the FlashMLA tests in #38 cover int64 positions.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR bumps FlashMLA to `d1a1c92` or removes this cast.

AI assistance (Codex, Claude Code) was used to implement and validate this change.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Use 32-row tiles in prepare_megamoe_inputs from 1024 tokens
