commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Stop preload groups when a daemon rank exits
commits.pr_body:
## Overview When a later preload rank exits after READY, the launcher can stay blocked joining an earlier, healthy rank and leave sibling daemons running. Supervise every rank through startup and serving, preserve the original failure status, and clean up the entire group. Related to #56049. ## Claims - Detect any rank's exit after READY without waiting for an earlier rank to exit first. - Preserve the failing rank's status before terminating siblings; report signal deaths as `128 + signal` and unexpected clean exits as status 1. - Terminate and reap started ranks on failure or launcher signals, escalating to `kill()` after a shared ten-second grace period. Stop the health endpoint during cleanup. ## Validation ### October 29 CI follow-up Upstream #64474 has now merged. This branch includes its original main commit `ee1056b3179adfd4523dfdceb87b0a079801b6f4`, with all four PR files byte-identical to the previous `6fdaec31fa3d` revision. On the exact merged head `2b53258c4ddc`, the same three B300 TP2 CLI fault scenarios passed again (**3 passed, 65 deselected, 70.19s**); all four feature-file hooks and merge commit hooks passed. On this same head, the hosted documentation build passed. Isotr0py requested `/ci retry`; [Buildkite #98305](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98305) reran the previously failing L4 Distributed Preload step successfully, with successful bootstrap, image-build and pre-commit checks. This is a targeted rerun, not a claim that the complete GPU matrix was rerun. Isotr0py enabled auto-merge; the last observed PR state remains OPEN. Current head: `2b53258c4ddcf89dc839228520a35cf8d669d906`; [test-only incremental diff](https://github.com/liusy58/vllm/compare/d7c8b710df9b194aae75cd87e4469d1e759a4457...6fdaec31fa3d8e7fbe23e87e8d8e4a226c5352b6). Isotr0py requested CI and marked the PR ready for review. The CI bot merged main `34091a07c7` as `d7c8b710df9b`. GitHub currently associates Isotr0py’s October 29 approval with `d7c8b710df9b194aae75cd87e4469d1e759a4457`. That approval predates the test-only follow-up below and is not represented as approval of the new revision or human-run validation. [Buildkite #98245, L4 Distributed Preload](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98245#01a18702-498d-499f-b395-803a9b0903fe) reported `2 failed, 3 passed` on `d7c8b710df9b`: the startup and serving tests raised `psutil.ZombieProcess` while reading `child.cmdline()`, before fault injection. A short-lived child can exit between enumeration and command-line inspection. The unresponsive-sibling case, existing TP2/EP model case and D2D warmup case passed in that job. The follow-up catches `psutil.NoSuchProcess` (including `ZombieProcess`) only while identifying live spawn children. It retains the exact two-rank requirement, launcher-aliveness/deadline checks, exit code 137 and sibling-reaping assertions. No new retry, skip, timeout relaxation or production change. - Deterministic real-process reproduction: extract the checked-in discovery block with Python AST, start two real multiprocessing spawn workers, and leave a third exited child unreaped using `waitid(WEXITED | WNOWAIT)`. On `d7c8b710df9b`, exit 1 with `psutil.ZombieProcess` at `cmdline()`; with the fix, exit 0 and the selected PID set equals exactly the two live workers. No mocks; all created processes are reaped afterwards. - B300 TP2, same three real CLI fault scenarios on `6fdaec31fa3d` after the fix: **3 passed, 65 deselected, 69.53s**. The unmodified merged head also passed locally in 86.19s; this does not erase the independently reproduced CI race. - Changed-file and commit hooks: passed. Local runs used GPUs 1 and 2, the existing PyTorch 2.13/cu130 environment and process-local CUDA 13.4 compatibility libraries. No checkpoint, assertion or shared-environment changes. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. \ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/liusy/codex-runtime/cuda-compat-13-4/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k preload_rank_failure -q ``` The [documentation build on the bot merge](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35493186/) separately failed on seven MiniMax-M3 AMD docstring cross-references (`head`, `:n`, `r`). All three affected files are byte-identical to the merged main. This was tracked by #64469 and fixed by the now-merged #64474, which is included through the upstream merge described above. No duplicate implementation was added. The included upstream fix is confirmed by the successful [hosted documentation build](https://vllm--63692.org.readthedocs.build/en/63692/); the targeted L4 revalidation also passed as recorded above. ### Original feature validation NVIDIA B300, real `vllm preload`, `facebook/opt-125m`, TP2. The three fault-injection cases kill the later rank during startup, after READY, and after READY with a sibling stopped by SIGSTOP. Only children created by the test are signalled, and final cleanup checks that no sibling is alive. | Check | Before | With fix | |---|---|---| | Same scenarios after merging main 2fb320d830 | 3 failed, 119.26s: same exit-code failure and two 30-second timeouts | 3 passed, 119.12s | | Current-main existing weight-cache unit cases | — | 60 passed, 48.26s | | Qwen3.5 ordinary + MTP model-output regression | — | 2 passed, 288.13s | | Changed-file and commit hooks | — | Passed | All passing results above are from head 6a5f3a50df after merging main 2fb320d830. The Qwen3.5 ordinary and MTP cases cover ordinary loading, disk fallback, IPC attachment and warm restart with the existing suite's configuration and assertions. An initial attempt failed when another user's workload occupied the selected GPU during the run: vLLM reported 61.77 GiB free against a 78.68 GiB IPC-engine budget. The unchanged tests passed on an idle GPU; the failed logs are retained. Runs emitted torch deprecation warnings. No multi-node or ROCm validation is claimed. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5,6 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k preload_rank_failure -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'not cold_start and not d2d_warmup and not preload_rank_failure' -q CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py -k 'cold_start_and_warm_restart and qwen' -q ``` For the new baseline run, the exact proposed test file was copied to `tests/model_executor/model_loader/_codex_supervision_baseline.py` in the compressed-FP8 worktree, whose `vllm/entrypoints/cli/preload.py` was verified byte-identical to main 2fb320d830. Running the first command against that temporary file yielded: ```text startup: AssertionError: assert 247 == (128 + SIGKILL) serving: subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 30 seconds unresponsive-sibling: subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 30 seconds 3 failed, 65 deselected, 14 warnings in 119.26s ``` The proposed source with the same tests yielded `3 passed, 65 deselected, 14 warnings in 119.12s`. Both runs used real CLI subprocesses and weights; baseline failures are expected reproductions, not skipped tests. ## Details The old serving path joins processes in creation order, so failure of a later rank does not wake a join on an earlier live rank. Startup also derives the exit status after terminating siblings, losing the original signal status. One supervision loop now checks all exits; after readiness it waits on process sentinels. A `finally` block cleans up the processes that actually started, including partial startup and explicit launcher shutdown. This is launcher failure handling, separate from the engine-side daemon-loss detection merged in #62734. It does not add automatic engine restart or the roadmap's proposed `--supervise` serving mode. The merge preserves the daemon-to-daemon seed configuration from #63088 and reuses the current test helper's log collection. The regression is selected by the existing distributed preload test steps; their dependencies now include the launcher source. The preload guide documents shutdown, failure status, and stale socket behavior after forced termination. No scheduler/model-runner changes or steady-state GPU synchronization. Duplicate checks on October 26 covered #56049 and its comments and open PR searches for preload supervision, rank exit, and weight-cache shutdown. No existing PR implements this launcher fix; #62734 addresses the separate engine lifetime contract, and #63088 adds daemon-to-daemon seeding. AI assistance: Codex implemented, merged, and ran the recorded validation at the submitter's request. The maintainer approval and subsequent test-only repair are distinguished above. No human-run tests or completed approval of the new repair are asserted. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses process sentinels and the existing launcher; no model-runner changes. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Real CLI before/after tests, existing units, earlier model-output regressions, and limits recorded above. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Changed-file hooks passed; preload docs and CI dependencies updated. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Motivation, duplicate checks, commands, evidence, limitations and AI disclosure included.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Reject chat templates for native renderers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Native Rust chat renderers (DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1, Harmony, Inkling, Kimi K3) do not render Jinja templates, but they silently ignored `--chat-template` and a request's `chat_template`. This PR rejects both instead: startup fails for the flag, and the request returns 400.

## Claims

- `--chat-template` with a resolved renderer other than `hf` fails at startup, naming the renderer and pointing to `--tokenizer-mode hf`.
- A request `chat_template` on a renderer other than `hf` returns 400 with `param: "chat_template"`.
- The `hf` renderer is unchanged: a request template still goes through the `--trust-request-chat-template` check.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --locked`: 1118 of 1119 passed. The one failure, `roundtrip_mimo_v26` (grammar replay snapshot), also fails on `main` at `ab0e5ef795` without this change.
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --lib --bins --tests --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: passed.
- `backend::hf::tests::only_hf_renderer_accepts_chat_template` covers both rejections and the unchanged `hf` path. Disabling either check makes it fail: the startup check returns `Ok`, and the request renders with the DeepSeek V4 encoder.

## Details

The startup check sits where `--tokenizer-mode` resolves the renderer. The request check uses a provided `ChatRenderer::renders_request_chat_template()` method that defaults to `false`, with `HfChatRenderer` returning `true`, so a new native renderer rejects request templates without opting in. `ChatRequestProcessor` checks it once before rendering, which covers chat completions, `/render`, and `/tokenize`.

Python is inconsistent here: Mistral rejects a request `chat_template` (`vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py`), while the DeepSeek tokenizers ignore it. This follows the Rust frontend's rule to reject behavior it does not implement. No recipe combines `--chat-template` with a native renderer.

This also replaces the GLM-only checks in vllm-project/vllm#62424, which used `ChatTemplateThrown` (meant for a template's `raise_exception`); that PR drops them.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs for chat-template rejection in native renderers and found none.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Benchmark] Count tool call deltas as generated tokens in openai-responses
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm bench serve --backend openai-responses` marks every tool-call-only response as failed. It counts only `output_text` and `reasoning_text` deltas as tokens, and a forced tool call streams only `function_call_arguments` deltas. This counts the four tool delta events the vLLM Responses server emits, as `openai-chat` counts `tool_calls` deltas.

## Claims

- 100 tool calls the server completed with HTTP 200 went from 0 to 100 successful, with totals now identical to `openai-chat` on the same workload.
- Added events: `function_call_arguments`, `custom_tool_call_input`, `mcp_call_arguments`, `code_interpreter_call_code` (from `responses/streaming_events.py`). Tool arguments are timed but not added to `generated_text`, as on chat.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py`: a tool-call-only response (TTFT, ITL, usage, `latency - ttft == sum(itl)`), each tool delta type, and text followed by a tool call. 30 passed; the 6 new ones fail on `main` with "Never received a token delta". Timing tests (29) and pre-commit pass.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, `tool_choice: "required"` via `--extra-body`:

| | `main` | this branch | `openai-chat` |
|---|---|---|---|
| completed / failed | 0 / 100 | 100 / 0 | 100 / 0 |
| input / output tokens | 0 / 0 | 20,610 / 2,090 | 20,610 / 2,090 |

Per request, output tokens match the server's `usage` and ITL counts match the token events recorded on the wire.

## Details

#54628 added this backend with tool calls out of scope. Leaving them out fails the request, so tool-calling workloads such as the BFCL dataset (#42457) can't be measured on it. The Rust `vllm-bench` Responses backend has the same gap; I'll send that separately.

No issue or PR covers this. Open PRs touching `endpoint_request_func.py` (#51155, #55719, #57519, #58734) don't change these events.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this and write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.

commits.pr_title: [Qwen4Exp] Remove FlashAttention dependency and standardize QSA naming
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Decouple Qwen4Exp QSA from FlashAttention backend, implementation, and metadata classes across NVIDIA and AMD. Retain the naming and metadata cleanup that makes indexer ownership explicit and removes redundant per-layer consistency checks.

## Claims

- Remove QSA's direct FlashAttention imports, inheritance, and availability probes while retaining its existing sparse-attention kernels and cache writers.
- Make the distinction between the QSA indexer and main attention explicit and consistent across implementations, warmup, and tests.
- Preserve computation, checkpoint parameter names, cache layouts, and public configuration for valid inputs.
- Retain builder-local validation while removing repeated cross-cache comparisons from forward paths. No performance improvement is claimed.

Continues the QSA/FlashAttention decoupling motivated by [#57395](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57395). Unlike that implementation, this change also replaces FlashAttention metadata/builders and preserves the current AMD FP8 and Octave paths. No overlapping naming-cleanup PR was found in upstream searches on 2026-10-28; related [#58449](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58449) and [#61529](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61529) address separate kernel/cache changes.

## Validation

Evaluated the same BF16 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoint before and after the change with TP4/EP, HC sequence parallelism, MTP3, and prefix caching disabled. GSM8K uses EvalScope 1.10.0, all 1,319 test questions, default 4-shot prompts, thinking enabled, greedy decoding, seed 1236, concurrency 32, and a 32,768-token generation limit. Each evaluation starts with fresh predictions.

| Main KV | Indexer dtype | Before cleanup | After cleanup | After FlashAttention removal |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 | BF16 | 1293/1319 (98.03%) | 1295/1319 (98.18%) | 1288/1319 (97.65%) |
| FP8 E4M3 | BF16 | 1291/1319 (97.88%) | 1294/1319 (98.10%) | 1292/1319 (97.95%) |
| BF16 | FP8 E4M3 | 1291/1319 (97.88%) | 1292/1319 (97.95%) | 1291/1319 (97.88%) |
| FP8 E4M3 | FP8 E4M3 | 1292/1319 (97.95%) | 1290/1319 (97.80%) | 1293/1319 (98.03%) |

The first two result columns cover the naming/metadata cleanup. The final column records fresh NVIDIA evaluations of all four configurations on the same merged code after FlashAttention removal.

All tested configurations started successfully, answered a 3,034-token sparse-attention prompt correctly, and completed GSM8K with zero response errors and zero truncations. Input prompts match question by question, and nonzero MTP acceptance confirms speculative decoding was exercised.

GSM8K accuracy remains broadly consistent with the pre-change baseline across the tested QSA configurations. Small run-to-run variation is observed even when evaluating unchanged code with the same settings.

- QSA reference/prepare suite and AMD test collection on CUDA: **90 passed, 23 skipped** (ROCm-only cases).
- Ruff check, format checks, whitespace checks, and repository static checks: passed.
- NVIDIA/AMD ops directories and the renamed common module's Triton kernel AST: unchanged.
- AMD imports and tests are updated and selected by existing CI; ROCm execution was not tested locally.

Test commands:

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare.py -q

evalscope eval --model qwen3.8-flash-next --api-url "$API_BASE/v1" \
  --api-key EMPTY_TOKEN --eval-type openai_api \
  --datasets gsm8k --eval-batch-size 32 --seed 1236 \
  --work-dir "$RESULTS_DIR" --no-timestamp \
  --generation-config '{"seed":1236,"do_sample":false,"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"top_k":-1,"repetition_penalty":1,"presence_penalty":1.5,"max_tokens":32768,"extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true}},"timeout":1800,"stream":true}'
```

## Details

1. **Removing FlashAttention dependency: use generic interfaces and QSA metadata.** QSA already runs its own sparse kernels, so remove FlashAttention inheritance and availability probes. Use `Qwen4ExpQSABackend(AttentionBackend)` / `Qwen4ExpQSAImpl(AttentionImplBase)` and shared `Qwen4ExpQSAMetadata` / `Qwen4ExpQSAMetadataBuilder` containing only batch bounds and cache addresses. Dispatch sparse attention through `forward` and reuse `reshape_and_cache_flash` for cache updates, retaining AMD's Octave writer/workspace setup and CUDA graph and draft-decode support.
2. **Module names: group code by indexer ownership.** Rename the NVIDIA/AMD `indexer_qsa.py` modules to `qsa_indexer.py`, matching the existing QSA indexer ops module. Rename the shared `qsa_cache.py` module to `qsa_indexer.py` because it owns metadata, a builder, a backend, and cache classes. This follows the indexer-centered organization used by GLM5Next's shared and platform implementations, for example [glm5next/nvidia/sparse_indexer.py:24](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/sparse_indexer.py#L24). Update imports and the warmup module lookup together so startup continues to find the renamed implementation.

3. **Metadata names: identify the component that consumes them.** Rename `QSAForwardMetadata` / `QSAMetadataBuilder` to `QSAIndexerMetadata` / `QSAIndexerMetadataBuilder`, and change `side_metadata` to `indexer_metadata`. These objects describe indexer cache addressing and selection, while main attention uses separate metadata. The naming follows `MiniMaxM3IndexerMetadata` / `MiniMaxM3IndexerMetadataBuilder` in [minimax_m3/common/indexer.py:186](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py#L186) and [indexer.py:205](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py#L205).

4. **Cache and backend names: describe ownership and stored data.** Rename `_QSAStateCache` / `QSAStateBackend` to `_QSAIndexerCache` / `QSAIndexerBackend`, consistent with `DeepseekV4IndexerCache` in [deepseek_v4/attention.py:886](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py#L886), `Glm5NextIndexerCache` in [glm5next/common/attention.py:79](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py#L79), and `MiniMaxM3IndexerBackend` in [minimax_m3/common/indexer.py:64](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py#L64). Rename `QSAKeyStateCache` to `QSARawKeyCache` to pair directly with `QSACompressedKeyCache` and distinguish raw keys from compressed keys. Update the internal backend identifier to `QWEN4_EXP_QSA_INDEXER` to match this ownership and remove the duplicated `EXP` segment.

5. **Field comments: make coordinate systems and units explicit.** Document that `logical_positions` uses original-token coordinates, `visible_blocks` counts complete compression groups, `k_work_metadata` contains compression tasks, and `storage_block_size` counts key rows per physical block. These distinctions matter because compressed rows and original tokens have different units. Keep explanations beside their fields, following the approach used for indexer split counts in [minimax_m3/common/indexer.py:193](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py#L193).

6. **Repeated checks: keep validation at the construction boundary.** Remove 32 lines comparing raw/compressed token counts, batch splits, logical positions, and main/indexer token counts. These values derive from the same batch inputs and builder rules, so every layer was repeating the same comparisons. Keep builder-local request-count, token-count, and uniform-decode checks, as well as independent cache-specific block tables and slot mappings. Deliberately inconsistent metadata loses the removed early errors; an independent batch ordering or token-trimming path would require revisiting this assumption. The removed `torch.equal` checks ran only on CPU tensors, so no GPU synchronization reduction is claimed.

AI assistance was used for code review, validation, and preparing this description. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing the change and reproducing the relevant tests.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Add native GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash chat rendering
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add native Rust GLM5Next chat rendering for GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, including tool calls and reasoning options. Rust `auto` selects it for the `glm5_next` model type (GLM-5.3-Flash); GLM-5.3 shares `glm_moe_dsa` with GLM-5 through GLM-5.2, so it uses `--tokenizer-mode glm5_next` explicitly.

## Claims

- Replace MiniJinja template interpretation with model-specific Rust rendering for both model templates.
- Produce token IDs with control markers resolved through the added vocabulary, while literal text uses the base vocabulary.

## Validation

After syncing upstream `main` through `94a29d316e` on 2026-10-25:

- `cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --lib --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1`: **442 chat tests and 510 server tests passed**.
- `cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1`: **93 CLI tests passed**.
- `cd rust && cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --lib --bins --tests --locked --offline -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Pre-commit checks on the resolved and changed files, Rust formatting, and the PR diff whitespace check passed.

The tests cover rendered prompts, complete token IDs, auto renderer selection, and in-process HTTP routes with the existing scripted engine. The final additional upstream Preload commit does not change the tested Rust or GLM configuration files.

<details>
<summary>Tool-choice regression: fails before the fix, passes after</summary>

The initial merged tree passed 441 chat tests but failed the existing GLM/HF prompt parity test: with `tool_choice="none"`, GLM omitted the tool definitions that HF rendered. The new HTTP render-route regression reproduced the same bug before removing the renderer's extra parsing gate:

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib --locked --offline render_glm_tools_for_none_follow_server_exclusion_setting -- --exact routes::tests::render_glm_tools_for_none_follow_server_exclusion_setting
```

```text
assertion `left == right` failed: exclude=false
  left: false
 right: true
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed
```

After the fix, both the existing GLM/HF parity test and the new route test pass in the suites above. The route test checks that tool definitions remain by default and are removed when `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none` is enabled. The Rust workspace Buildkite job selects this test.

</details>

Previous author-reported frontend benchmarks compared both templates against HF MiniJinja with identical requests, 4 server CPU cores, concurrency 64, and two 4-second runs per configuration:

| Workload | Native / HF throughput |
| --- | --- |
| Short tool conversations | 1.50x |
| Parallel tool calls | 1.75–1.79x |
| Long tool histories | 1.77–1.86x |

These measurements cover frontend rendering and tokenization, excluding model inference, and were not rerun for this upstream sync. GPU serving and model evaluations were not rerun on the local macOS host.

## Details

This PR adds chat rendering; multimodal preprocessing is owned by `llm-multimodal`, with the GLM processor work handled in [smg-project/smg#4036](https://github.com/smg-project/smg/pull/4036). The Python frontend continues to use the HF tokenizer and renderer. The tokenizer-mode docstring generates the user-facing argument reference, both GLM recipes include deployment examples, and the tool-calling guide documents the default tool-definition policy for the native GLM renderer.

Both `glm5_next` and upstream's `alpamayo2_super` tokenizer modes are preserved. GLM tool definitions follow the effective tool list; the server owns the exclusion policy, rather than the renderer's tool-parsing flag. Chat Completions conversion retains empty explicit reasoning strings; `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` are vLLM extensions absent from the OpenAI OpenAPI 2.3.0 assistant-message schema checked on 2026-10-25.

Rejecting `--chat-template` and request `chat_template` for native renderers, including `glm5_next`, is handled generically in vllm-project/vllm#64274.

Duplicate-work check: this continues the existing native GLM renderer PR; the earlier GLM/Rust/tokenizer search found no other PR implementing the same renderer.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Kimi-K3: move the GB300 AgentX presets to the Oct 26 points with KV-balanced decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Update the two GB300 Kimi-K3 AgentX disaggregated presets in `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml` to the lanes qualified in [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4638](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4638) (head `bc4d49f5`, sweep run [40830592414](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40830592414), attempt 1): `kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg` (preset `gb300_agentx_pd`) and `kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dep16-disagg` (preset `gb300_agentx_pd_dep16`). Both lanes now run image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev229+g3966924d5` in the run logs) with Dynamo `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`, and their throughput points run decode attention on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`. Each preset now has one `points.` per measured operating point, and the worker commands, environment block and Mooncake connector move out of the runbooks into structured fields. No open PR updates these lanes or their points; #64586 (drop dead envs from Kimi-K3) and #64617 (a B300 preset) edit the same file, so whichever merges second needs a rebase. ## Claims **`gb300_agentx_pd` (AgentX xPyD, default on GB300 `pd_cluster`, as before):** - `source` is #4638 at `bc4d49f5df307680be5a1567e01b838b83b31b62`. The image is pinned by digest (`@sha256:f255c4fa…`), and the Dynamo commit is unchanged. - There are 10 points with stable ids, one per measured point, matching the lane's search space: - **Specialized decode** (`TOKENSPEED_MLA`, `latency_specialized`, `--max-num-seqs 12`): `1p3d_c16`, `1p2d_c24` (the default point, as the preset rendered before) and `1p2d_c32`. - **Regular decode** (`KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`): `2p4d_c112`, `2p4d_c128`, `2p3d_c128`, `2p3d_c152`, `3p4d_c240`, `3p3d_c240` and `3p3d_c264`. - The 1P2D c48/c64 and 2P3D c240 points are no longer run, so they are dropped. - Regular points use these settings: - **Both roles:** BF16 SSM state and FlashInfer autotune on. - **Decode:** `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`, with the DSpark draft's `attention_backend` on the same backend; `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv: 8` in `--attention-config`; `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512` and `--use-replayssm`; vLLM's default CUDA graph mode. - **Prefill:** stays on `TOKENSPEED_MLA` for target and draft. - Specialized points keep the earlier profile on both roles: FP32 SSM state, `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1` and autotune off. - Both roles move the NIXL + Mooncake store `MultiConnector` from the runbook into structured fields. It comes from `select.kv_offload: kv_store_distributed_mooncake`, with `json_args` for the lane's connector options: recompute on failed loads, `kv_buffer_device: cuda`, `enforce_handshake_compat: false`, `enable_cross_layers_blocks: false` and `enable_offload: false`. - The decode role drops the DEP-only `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` and `--no-enable-prefix-caching` with `remove_args`, replacing the earlier undo flags. - Environment additions on both roles, as the lane sets them: `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0` on decode too, `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120` and `ETCD_LEASE_TTL=600`. - Prefill KV events (`--kv-events-config`) are removed, because the lane no longer publishes them. **`gb300_agentx_pd_dep16` (AgentX 3P1D DEP16, opt-in):** - `source` is #4638 at the same commit, and the image is the same digest-pinned image. - The decode role runs target and draft attention on `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`. Prefill stays on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`. - There are three points, `c256`, `c288` and `c336` (default). The lane runs one configuration at all three client counts. - The KV connector comes from the same `select` + `json_args`. The decode role also sets the store child to `kv_consumer` with `enable_lookup: false`. - Prefill KV events are removed. **Runbooks** keep the evidence and processes the builder does not render: - the worker-count table; - multi-tray launch notes; - the specialized-decode and KV-balanced notes; - the Dynamo parser flags; - the etcd/NATS/Mooncake master commands and the lane's store configuration (160GB per rank, 60 s lease); - the frontend (`least-loaded`, session affinity). The duplicated Workers/Environment command blocks are removed. `meta.date_updated` is set to 2026-10-29. ## Validation - `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir /recipes` passes (vllm-project/recipes @ `2ac6bc4`): 220 recipes, JSON API built. - I built the full JSON API before and after the change. Only Kimi-K3 family files change: - `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.json` and its promoted variants `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-NVFP4`, `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-FP8-BLOCK` and `Eco-Tech/Kimi-K3-w4a8` (only `presets` and `meta.date_updated` change); - `presets/gb300_agentx_pd.json` and `presets/gb300_agentx_pd_dep16.json`; - the three `hw/gb300/strategies/pd_cluster.json` files. No `strategy_overrides`, hardware or variant field changes, so the Baseline (non-preset) commands are unchanged on every GPU and strategy. The default GB300 `pd_cluster` rendering (default preset, point `1p2d_c24`) changes only in: - the digest-pinned image; - the Mooncake `MultiConnector` with `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` and `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, which the builder's Mooncake option adds; - the dropped DEP undo flags; - the env additions above. - **Against the source:** every one of the 13 rendered points matches the lane's effective arguments and environment on both roles at the PR head. The script merges `disagg-variants.yaml` / `disagg-tp8-dep16.yaml` base roles with each point's override and checks against the master config's search space: concurrency, prefill and decode worker counts, two trays per TP8 worker and four per DEP16 worker, and the image. The only flags the builder adds are restatements of the lane's effective values: - `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`; - `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` on the xPyD pools; - `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb` on the DEP16 decode, which the lane's per-node DP launch also adds; - `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` next to `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` on the specialized prefill. - **Against the logs:** the rendered `2p4d_c112` and `c256` prefill and decode commands and environment match the launch commands logged in run 40830592414 (2P4D c112 and 3P1D c256 eval jobs), apart from placement, parser and InferenceX plumbing (listed below). The worker logs show: - decode `Using AttentionBackendEnum.KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA backend` (32x per job) and prefill on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`; - `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` on both xPyD roles; - the prefill CUDA graph mode `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. - **Accuracy**, from the sweep's eval jobs with block verification: Kimi tool-call schema `em_strict` 0.985-0.998 (n=408) at every point, and GSM8K `em_strict` 0.966-0.972 (n=1319) where run. ## Details **Schema limitations:** - **Worker counts:** the builder renders one prefill and one decode worker per pool, so the xPyD counts (for example 2P4D) cannot be expressed. Each point's label, description and the runbook table give them. Role `nodes` stays at two trays per TP8 worker, because a larger `nodes` would render one wider TP group instead of more workers. - **Mooncake master and store sizing:** the master options and store sizing are not preset fields. The builder's Mooncake option shows its own defaults (100GB segment, 30 s lease), so the runbook gives the lane's values. - **Router and session affinity:** the Dynamo frontend's router mode and session affinity are not builder fields. **`gb300_low_latency` is unchanged.** The #4638 aggregated `dcp8-agg` c1 point is an image-only bump, and its serving flags already match that preset's `tp16` point, apart from the image and the synthetic acceptance. A point can pin its own `image`, but `source` (href/key/revision) exists only on the preset, and that preset cites vllm-project/recipes#1134 with the rolling `nightly` image for both its points. Citing the InferenceX key would mean re-sourcing or splitting that preset, so I left it. **Excluded as InferenceX-only, placement or no-op:** - **Benchmark controls:** concurrency lists, synthetic acceptance (`rejection_sample_method: synthetic`, `synthetic_acceptance_length` on throughput runs; the presets keep block verification), AIPerf/trace-replay settings, `dram-utilization` and Tachometer (disabled in #4638). - **Harness plumbing:** `--served-model-name` and the local `/model` path, `--device-ids`, `--dump-config-to`, `--request-plane tcp` (the builder sets `DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp`), Slurm/container/health-check settings, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, `TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES`, `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM`, `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`, the per-host Mooncake/NIXL/OTEL addresses, and `NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST` (a site value; the runbook says to set it). - **Eval-only parsers:** `--dyn-tool-call-parser`, `--dyn-reasoning-parser` and `--dyn-enable-structural-tag`, which the runbook documents. - **No-op envs:** `VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT` and `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL`. The lane sets them, but vLLM at the pinned commit `3966924d` reads neither (`git grep` finds no reference under `vllm/`), and `prefix_cache_retention_interval` already defaults to 0 (`vllm/config/cache.py`). #64586 removes them from the other Kimi-K3 presets. **Known renderer behaviour:** like the other presets that tune a composed connector by name, the `json_args` on `--kv-transfer-config` assume the Mooncake store selected by the preset. If a user turns that KV offload option off while the preset is active, the renderer raises an error for the missing `MooncakeStoreConnector` child. ### Generated preset JSON, before and after Condensed: the default point in full (`docker_*`/`command` fields and per-host env omitted), then each other point's differences from it.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO: hybrid READ for several attention groups and shared-group speculative methods
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) cannot run MoRIIO hybrid READ P/D on `main`. It has two transferable attention groups (MLA + indexer, and the kpool tail ring, a `CircularBufferSpec`), KDA groups, and MTP. `main` allows one attention group and DSpark only. With the packed `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` layout, `main` also classifies KDA groups as attention and silently skips recurrent-state transfer.

Changes (connector-only: `moriio_connector.py`, tests, one docs line):

- Hybrid READ payload is `[*attn_groups, *mamba_groups]`, byte-identical to `main` with one attention group.
- `_align_read_blocks` runs per attention group. Non-prefix-cacheable groups are read even on a full local hit.
- Each hybrid layer is routed to its own payload group. READ destinations of all attention groups are excluded from KV zeroing.
- A group is Mamba when every layer spec it covers is a `MambaSpec`.
- READ: the DSpark-only check is replaced by "the drafter shares the target's attention groups" (MTP, DSpark). Hybrid WRITE (#60544) is unchanged, including its DSpark check.
- `CircularBufferSpec` is accepted only for hybrid READ. Non-hybrid and hybrid WRITE still fail closed (`NotImplementedError` at init).
- Usage guide: drop the single-attention-group requirement.

Scope:

- Non-hybrid models do not reach the changed code (all scheduler changes are under `_has_mamba`).
- Single-attention-group hybrid READ is covered by byte-identity unit tests only.
- Drafters with a separate attention group are out of scope.

Requires #58585 (per-layer `block_len`), merged. The branch includes `main` with #60544 (hybrid WRITE).

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
```

Environment: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, MI300X.

E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, 1P/1D, MoRIIO READ, MTP 1, EP8 per leg, KV block 8, MI300X; `main` 19b0efce30 + this PR only.

## Test Result

### Unit

- On the merge with `main` a7407ab445 (incl. #62473): all `test_moriio_*.py` 878 passed, 0 failed (872 on `main`).
- Two `main` tests are intentionally replaced: the multiple-attention-group rejection and the READ case of the non-DSpark rejection.
- New tests: GLM-5.3-Flash grouping with MTP, payload pairing (partial/full hit), per-layer routing, single-group byte-identity, no-attention-group gate, `CircularBufferSpec` rejection (non-hybrid, hybrid WRITE), WRITE non-DSpark rejection. The non-hybrid gate test fails on the previous head.

### E2E without this PR

All 8 engine cores per leg fail at connector init; servers never come up:

```
moriio_connector.py, line 519, in __init__
MoRIIOError: MoRIIO hybrid READ requires exactly one transferable attention group, got 2; ...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Baseline below is therefore the prefill server queried directly (no KV transfer).

### E2E with this PR

Random data, 1024 output tokens, 16 requests at c=1, 32 at c=8, no failures. Cells: run 1 / run 2, different node pairs.

| ISL, concurrency | TTFT mean (ms) | TTFT P99 (ms) | TPOT mean (ms) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K, c=1 | 1329 / 1262 | 2459 / 1943 | 9.8 / 10.0 | 90.3 / 88.9 |
| 8K, c=8 | 1720 / 1615 | 2962 / 2907 | 11.2 / 11.2 | 554 / 587 |
| 32K, c=1 | 3705 / 3626 | 3759 / 3685 | 10.4 / 10.1 | 71.5 / 73.4 |
| 32K, c=8 | 7052 / 6228 | 10915 / 10011 | 11.6 / 11.7 | 385 / 396 |
| 256K, c=1 | 31952 / 31517 | 32973 / 32512 | 8.8 / 9.3 | 25.0 / 24.9 |
| 512K, c=1 | 66391 / 65961 | 67178 / 67412 | 9.9 / 9.4 | 13.4 / 13.6 |

Run-to-run TTFT variation: 0.6–2.2% at c=1 (32K–512K), 6–12% at c=8.

| Check (run 1 / run 2) | P/D router | Prefill direct |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, strict | 91.21 ± 0.78 / 91.89 ± 0.75 | 92.27 ± 0.74 / 92.57 ± 0.72 |
| NIAH found/10, seeds 0/1/2, 2K / 8K / 32K words | run 1: 10,10,10 / 10,10,9 / 1,10,10; run 2: 10,10,10 / 10,10,10 / 10,9,10 | all 10 (32K: one run) |
| 16-concurrent NIAH × 3 rounds | 48/48 / 48/48 | – |
| Single needle, 243K/486K/713K tokens × 3 depths | 7/9 / 9/9 | – |
| MTP acceptance during GSM8K | 93.4% / 93.3% | 95.1% / 95.1% |

- After merging `main` 5be4266f5c (2 runs): GSM8K 90.90 ± 0.79 / 91.96 ± 0.75; 16-concurrent NIAH 48/48 both; NIAH 2K 9,10,9 / 10,10,9, 8K 10,10,10 / 8,10,10, 32K 3,10,10 / 8,10,10.
- After merging `main` a7407ab445 (incl. #62473, #62102), on a rebuilt image (ROCm 7.2.3, AITER v0.1.26): 8+8 engines up, 2 attention + 3 Mamba groups, 34 KDA layers, no `MoRIIOError`; NIAH 2K 10,10,10, 8K 10,10,10, 32K 1,10,9; 16-concurrent NIAH 48/48; GSM8K 91.51 ± 0.77.
- Without the packed-Mamba classification fix, NIAH was 0/10 at 2K words for 2 of 3 seeds.

Caveats:

- GSM8K router minus prefill-direct, paired by question: -1.06 (95% CI -2.37 to +0.25) and -0.68 (95% CI -1.78 to +0.42). Both include zero.
- NIAH misses are not transfer-related: on the merged tree, 2K words × 5 seeds × 3 passes, 4/15 prefill-direct and 3/15 router requests missed a needle, and same-path reruns flip between complete and incomplete (temperature 0).
- MTP acceptance is 1.7–1.8 points lower via P/D.
- No `MoRIIOError` or tracebacks on either leg in any run.

Note: the KV-connector and MoRIIO CI jobs are currently disabled on `main` (#63609), so CI on this head did not run them; the MoRIIO unit results above are from our MI300X cluster.

AI assistance (Claude) was used in preparing this change.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Bump Transformers version to 5.22.0
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bump Transformers to [v5.22.0](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases/tag/v5.22.0). Follows #64049.

## Claims

- `requirements/common.txt` allows `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.23.0`, and CI pins 5.22.0.
- The only breaking change in 5.22 (huggingface/transformers#49679, EP styles moved out of `tensor_parallel.py`) does not touch vLLM: nothing imports `transformers.distributed` or the moved classes.
- 5.22 adds a native `RadioModel` (`q/k/v_proj`, `o_proj`), which vLLM's RADIO loader already maps, so only `test_radio.py` needed updating. Its weight-loading test also compared uninitialized (possibly NaN) parameters, which is fixed here too.

## Validation

- No tests are gated on 5.22 (`min_transformers_version`/skip markers).
- `test_radio.py` on B200 with 5.22: 10 passed.
- Qwen2.5-VL PPL on B200: 22.2441 (+0.30%) on both 5.21.1 and 5.22, so the PPL job's failure is not from this bump.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_radio.py

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Check skinny-GEMM guard dispatch without torch.profiler
commits.pr_body:
- Detect whether `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` took the skinny path by wrapping `ops.wvSplitK`, instead of reading kernel names from `torch.profiler`
- Drop the profiler capture retry loop and the kernel-name matchers that worked around empty captures
- Check numerics on the same call whose dispatch was asserted, under both caps

The four dispatch tests added in #63179 fail with `kernels=[]` on the daily Full CI run on MI300 ([build 98403](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98403#01a188d7-e91a-4a6f-82cf-7640a13143d4), both attempts) but pass on per-commit builds. Only the daily run arms the kernel recorder from vllm-project/ci-infra#685, which registers its own ROCProfiler SDK tool through `ROCP_TOOL_LIBRARIES`. With that set, the SDK configures only the listed tool. Kineto's `rocprofiler_configure` in `libtorch_cpu.so` never registers, and `torch.profiler` records nothing, not even a plain `a @ a`. The guard's contract is which branch runs, so the test now checks that directly, regardless of what else is profiling the process.

Validation on MI355X, with the ci-infra recorder built from source and armed the way the daily run arms it:

- Before: `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_lmhead_skinny_gemm_guard.py` passes 9/9 without the recorder and fails the same 4 tests as CI with it.
- After: 9/9 passed in 10/10 runs without the recorder, 10/10 with it, and with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.
- Mutation check: removing the guard from the dispatch fails `test_n5_big_weight_dispatch[None-False]`; removing the n=1 carve-out fails `test_n1_big_weight_dispatch_unchanged`.
- Full `pytest -v -s model_executor -m '(not slow_test) and (not distributed)'` under the recorder: 1403 passed, 90 skipped, 0 failed (same count as per-commit CI).

No open PR touches this test (searched `test_lmhead_skinny_gemm_guard`, `skinny gemm guard`, `kernrec`). MI300 was not available locally; the CI group runs there.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Skip AITER tuned GEMM when M*N >= 2^31 on gfx950
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip AITER's tuned GEMM (`tgemm.mm`) on gfx950 when M·N ≥ 2^31 (Also skip AITER tuned GEMM when A or B spans >= 4 GiB) and fall back to `F.linear` (hipBLASLt). This works around an int32 output-offset overflow in AITER's gfx950 FlyDSL A16W16 kernel (fix pending in ROCm/aiter#6853). Since AITER v0.1.26, that overflow crashes `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` at startup with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.

## Claims

- Fixes the `Memory access fault ... Write access to a read-only page` crash during the encoder-cache profile run of MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on MI355X (TP4) with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`.
- No performance cost: only GEMMs with ≥ 2^31 output elements are rerouted, and hipBLASLt matches the FlyDSL kernel's throughput at those sizes. Normal LLM prefill/decode GEMMs never reach this size.

## Validation

Environment: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, AITER 0.1.26.

**Kernel-level repro** (`tgemm.mm` vs `F.linear`, N=6144, K=1280, bf16, with bias; this matches the tuned `minimax_m3_mxfp4_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` rows):

| M | M·N vs 2^31 | `tgemm.mm` (AITER) | `F.linear` (hipBLASLt) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 340,000 | below | 1221 TFLOP/s | 1206 TFLOP/s |
| 360,000 | above | Memory access fault | n/a |
| 768,000 | above | Memory access fault | 1229 TFLOP/s |

**End-to-end** with this patch:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 -tp 4 --trust-remote-code --block-size 128 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --moe-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 
```

Before: crashes at startup with the memory access fault. After: startup completes (178 GiB KV cache on TP0), and three chat requests with a 2016×2016 image return 200 with no faults. Confirmed there is no accuracy change.

No unit test is added: reproducing the bug needs gfx950 hardware plus AITER's model-specific tuned CSV, and a mocked test would only restate the condition.

## Details

**Root cause.** With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, each rank runs the ViT unsharded, so the profile run issues an M=768000, N=6144, K=1280 GEMM with bias. In AITER v0.1.26, `getPaddedM` maps it to the `8192,6144,1280` FlyDSL row in `minimax_m3_mxfp4_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv`. That kernel computes `global_row * n + global_col` in int32, which wraps once M·N ≥ 2^31 and writes out of bounds. In TP mode N is sharded 4 ways, so M·N stays under the limit.

**Why route around it here.** `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` is the only vLLM call site of `tgemm.mm`. The guard is limited to gfx950 and to the exact overflow condition, so all other shapes keep AITER's tuned dispatch. Skipping FlyDSL for this call also avoids the FlyDSL 0.4.0 `from_dlpack` leak described in ROCm/aiter#6853, which pinned about 10.6 GiB after the ViT profile run.

The guard can be removed once vLLM's minimum AITER includes ROCm/aiter#6853.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Build the SWA decode metadata in one launch
commits.pr_body:
## Overview With `--monokernel` on gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4.1 decode batches of up to 32 rows now build their SWA metadata with `swa_decode_meta`'s single Triton launch (#60731). Before, they took vLLM's 8 launches per SWA group. #60731 enabled the kernel only on gfx942, but the kernel has no arch-specific code. This PR converges with #63994: it takes #63994's gate, `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` (`on_gfx942() or on_gfx950()`), and adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step and the GPU validation below. ## Claims - **49 fewer launches per decode step at c1: 114 to 65.** That is 7 SWA groups (4 target, 3 DSpark draft), each going from 8 launches to 1. Counted in a torch-profiler trace of each arm. - **Decode step (ITL p50): c1 -100 us (-1.75%), c2 -80 us (-1.16%).** - Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X TP4, `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6 (synthetic AL 3.87, AV off), 32k in / 1k out, on `main` nightly 5d35ce3934. - Runs: 2 rounds with the arms' GPU halves swapped. The per-round deltas are -1.85% and -1.66% at c1, and -1.70% and -0.61% at c2. - **Same metadata, same accuracy.** - On MI355X, the kernel test matches vLLM's ops. - With AV off, GSM8K matches base at 4 parallel requests, where every decode-only step takes the new path (6 runs per arm), and at 8 parallel (10 runs per arm). - Acceptance length (AL) on first passes and on passes with a per-request `cache_salt` is 3.577 in both arms. - With AV on (1 server per arm), GSM8K and AL match as well. - **Unchanged:** gfx942, runs without `--monokernel`, other arches, and prefill, mixed or >32-row batches. The gate test covers arch x flag; the row and prefill guards are #60731's and untouched. There is no new flag. ## Validation **Tests (MI355X, gfx950)** | Test | This PR | Before (PR base) | |---|---|---| | `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py`: kernel vs vLLM's ops, 300 random batches per case | `-k swa_decode_meta`: 2 passed; whole file: 3 passed | (kernel unchanged) | | `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, with the new gate test (arch x `--monokernel`) | 82 passed | 81 passed, 1 failed: `[gfx950-True]` `assert [] == [False]` | | Extra, not in the PR: the kernel test with the target's 7 rows per request (k=6), the k=6 draft block, and 4 seeds x 500 batches | 8 passed: 4,000 batches; target rows 1-4 and 7/14/21/28, draft rows 6/12/18/24 at width 192 | | - **CI:** - The kernel test (`-k swa_decode_meta`) is added to `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`. Until now CI ran it only in the MI300 (gfx942) kernels step. - The gate test runs in the existing `(MI355) Basic Models (Other)` mirror. It stubs `launch` and the platform, so no CI job runs `build()` with the real kernel on gfx950. The trace and the GSM8K runs below cover that path outside CI. - **Other checks:** - On MI355X, the gate test kills 6 of 6 gate mutants: `on_mi3xx()` in place of the arch check, gfx942 only, any ROCm arch, no `--monokernel` check, no `cache_clear()`, and `build()` back on `enabled()`. - pre-commit passes on the 5 files at the first commit, and ruff passes on the second. - The PR applies cleanly to current `main`. **Performance.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, one TP4 server per half of the node. The servers run `--monokernel` with DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87 and AV off. The workload is random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, 32 prompts per run, 3 runs per point on the same server. The decode step is ITL p50. | ITL p50 (ms), each cell base / PR | Round 1 (base on GPUs 0-3) | Round 2 (base on GPUs 4-7) | Mean base | Mean PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | c1 | 5.687 / 5.581 | 5.681 / 5.587 | 5.684 | 5.584 | **-100 us (-1.75%)** | | c2 | 6.917 / 6.800 | 6.865 / 6.824 | 6.891 | 6.812 | **-80 us (-1.16%)** | - **Noise:** - The 3 runs on one server span up to 0.3% at c1 and up to 1.0% at c2 (max-min). - The same arm moves 0.1% between GPU halves at c1 and up to 0.75% at c2. - **Image:** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`. That is the PR base, which already has #63576, plus 23 commits. - The PR arm is the same image with the PR's 3 vllm files copied in. The end-to-end runs used the first commit. The second only swaps `on_mi3xx()` for `on_gfx942() or on_gfx950()`, which give the same value on gfx942 and gfx950 (`_ON_MI3XX` is exactly those two arches). The tests above ran on the second commit. - Those files are byte-identical between the PR base and 5d35ce3934. - AV-on perf was not measured. **Launch counts.** These come from a torch-profiler trace of each arm: rank 0, c1, 133 decode steps each. The SWA-build kernel counts are the same on every step. The total, fill and copy counts below are the per-step mode; a few steps add the same extra launches in both arms. The PR is 49 launches lower on every step. | Per decode step | base | PR | |---|---:|---:| | All launches (eager kernels plus graph launches): 115 of 133 steps; the others are 117/133 for base, 68/84 for PR | 114 | 65 | | `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` (target) and the draft's non-causal index kernel | 4 + 3 | 0 | | `torch.ge` (`compare_scalar_kernel`) / `FillFunctor` | 7 / 9 | 0 / 2 | | `_count_valid_row_entries_kernel` / rocprim scan / `_compact_dense_row_to_ragged_kernel` | 7 / 7 / 7 | 0 / 0 / 0 | | `__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer` | 24 | 10 | | `_decode_swa_meta_kernel` | 0 | 7 | | **SWA metadata launches.** The fill and copy rows also hold 2 fills and 10 copies per step outside the SWA build, in both arms. | **56** | **7** | | `_token_request_mapping_kernel` (control) | 2 | 2 | | GPU time per step (median, profiler on). Base: the target index, compare, count, scan and compact kernels; the draft index kernels, fills and copies are not counted. PR: `_decode_swa_meta_kernel`. | 136.5 us | 36.8 us | **Accuracy and AL** (AV off unless noted). GSM8K-1319 is 8-shot at temperature 0, over `/v1/completions`. AL is real block-rejection acceptance, read from `/metrics`. | GSM8K-1319 | base | PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 4 parallel: every decode-only step takes the new path. 6 runs per arm on 4 servers. | 0.9143 | 0.9151 | +0.0008 | | 8 parallel: steps with 5 or more requests keep vLLM's build. 10 runs per arm on 4 servers. | 0.9146 | 0.9123 | -0.0023 (SE 0.0022). Per-server means: -0.006, below the 0.0077 binomial SE of a single run. | | Mono forced off, so the aiter attention reads the kernel's ragged views. 4 parallel, 2 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9132 | 0.9143 | +0.0011 | | Mono forced off, 8 parallel (mostly vLLM's views). 4 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9166 | 0.9177 | +0.0011 | | AV on, 8 parallel: 2 runs per arm, 1 server each | 0.9143 | 0.9166 | +0.0023 | | AV on, 4 parallel: 1 run per arm | 0.9227 | 0.9158 | -0.0068 (per-run sd is about 0.005) | | AL with AV off, on a first pass (only the shared 8-shot prefix cached) or with a per-request `cache_salt` (nothing cached). 8 runs per arm: 6 at 8 parallel, 2 at 4 parallel. | 3.577 | 3.577 | 0 | | AL with AV on, first pass | 3.373 | 3.383 | +0.010 | - **Run-to-run variation:** - Any two AV-off runs with mono on, at the same parallelism, on the same server or not, differ on 53-88 of the 1319 questions (53-92 including the mono-off runs). - Greedy decode on this stack is not run-to-run deterministic on either arm. The first token can differ even with a fresh `cache_salt`, so a text-identity check was not possible. - **The mono-off rows:** - With `--monokernel`, mono consumes only the dense indices and lengths. - The 4-parallel mono-off row is therefore the end-to-end check of the ragged indices, `indptr` and `is_valid_token`. **Sync check.** One TP4 server per arm ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which polices the worker's `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` after warmup. Each served c1 and c2 (8 requests each, 512 out), 300 GSM8K questions at 4 parallel requests, and 4 greedy probes. Neither arm reported a sync, logged an error or failed a request.
Reproduction commands ```bash IMG=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9 # PR arm: the same image with this PR's 3 files copied over # /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/{ops/__init__.py,ops/swa_decode_meta.py,rocm.py} # Mono-off arms: in .../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py, in _decode_step, change # `if not 1 <= rows <= _max_rows():` to `if True:`, so mono declines every step. # Server, 4x MI355X, inside the image VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \ VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \ --max-model-len 1048576 --block-size 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' # Accuracy servers: "rejection_sample_method":"block", without synthetic_acceptance_length. # AV-on round: "enable_adaptive_verification":true. # Perf: warm up (c2, 4 prompts, 256 out, seed 7), then run each point 3 times: vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 # c2: --max-concurrency 2 --seed 102 # GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt and scoring, 8 shots, 1319 questions, temperature 0, max 512 tokens, # 8 or 4 parallel requests. # AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total) # Uncached passes: a unique "cache_salt" per request. # Tests on MI355X pytest tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py -k swa_decode_meta pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # Fail-before: keep the new test, restore the pre-PR vllm files, re-run. git checkout $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/__init__.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/swa_decode_meta.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # 81 passed, 1 failed ([gfx950-True]) ```
## Details **Change.** `ops.swa_decode_meta_enabled()`, the gate from #63994, returns true with `--monokernel` on ROCm when `on_gfx942()` or `on_gfx950()` holds. Only `swa_decode_meta.build` uses it. The other gfx942 helpers keep `ops.enabled()`. On gfx942 the two gates agree. **Limits.** - The kernel takes at most 32 rows; gfx950 mono takes up to 48. - With AV off at k=6, steps with 5 or more requests keep vLLM's build: the target at 35 or more rows, and the draft, which is padded to the 36-row graph. gfx942 behaves the same. - With AV on, the cutoff is 32 rows, not a request count. - AV-on `--monokernel` deployments now take this path. The AV-on round served without errors and matched base on accuracy and AL. **Related PRs.** - **#63994** (cpersson-amd) made the same change, and the two are converged here. This PR takes #63994's `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` gate, with Carl Persson as co-author of that commit. It adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step (#63994 used the optional `test-amd.yaml` step) and the GPU validation. #63994 can be closed. - **#58352:** it does not conflict textually, but the gains overlap. If it lands first, about 20 of the 49 launches remain (inferred, not measured). - **#61311** touches 4 of this PR's 5 files: `models_basic.yaml`, `ops/__init__.py`, `rocm.py` and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. - It renames `KernelConfig.monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `specialized_decode`, and replaces `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` with `test_dsv41_specialized_decode.py`. - Whichever lands second rebases: rename `_monokernel` in `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` and move the gate test. - **#63486 (draft)** moves the DSv4.1 mono CI and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. If it lands first, I drop the `models_basic.yaml` hunk and move the gate test. - **#63891 (draft)** runs fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with `--monokernel`. It adds its own `mi3xx_enabled()` on `on_mi3xx()`, and the same review applies to it. Both PRs touch the same `models_basic.yaml` step and the `ops/__init__.py` docstring; the second to land merges those hunks.
Why the metadata is the same, and who reads it - **What the kernel writes.** `_decode_swa_meta_kernel` is integer Triton with no arch intrinsics. - For rows `[0, n)` it writes `is_valid_token` and the dense window indices and lengths. It sets the lengths from row `n` to the end of the buffer to 0. It writes `indptr[:n+1]` and the ragged indices up to `indptr[n]`. - These are the same values that `torch.ge`, the length fill, `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` (or `ComputeDSparkNoncausalSWAIndicesKernel` for the draft block), `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` and `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers` produce. - `build()` returns views of the same persistent buffers, with the same lengths: ragged `[:max(n*width, 1)]` and `indptr[:n+1]`. - **Who reads it.** - **Mono:** with `--monokernel`, every target and DSpark-draft layer runs mono on decode-only steps of 48 rows or fewer that replay a FULL graph or run eagerly. Mono reads only the dense indices and lengths, `slot_mapping` and `token_to_req`. - **aiter sparse MLA:** on steps that mono declines, such as PIECEWISE steps, it (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`) reads the ragged indices between `indptr[t]` and `indptr[t+1]`. It sizes its splits from the ragged view's `numel()`, which is `n*width` on both paths. - **Top-k build:** it reads `is_valid_token` on compressed layers. - Draft and target builders do not share buffers. - **The only bytes that differ** are the ragged entries past `indptr[n]`. vLLM's build copies them from a `torch.empty` tensor; the kernel leaves the previous contents. No reader reads past `indptr`. - **#60154** is on `main` but not in the measured image. It fuses inverse RoPE and the MXFP8 quant into the aiter sparse-MLA output, and does not change the index views that call reads. So this argument holds on current `main`.
An AL caveat for anyone reproducing (affects main, not this PR) On 4 of the 10 AV-off servers, AL fell from about 3.58 to 3.42-3.45 on GSM8K passes that repeated the same prompts. Those passes had about 96% prefix-cache hits, against about 89% on a first pass. The 4 servers were 2 base and 2 PR; one of the PR servers had mono forced off. - The two dropped servers that ran later passes stayed low. - On the one dropped server that also ran passes with a per-request `cache_salt`, those passes stayed at 3.58. - Accuracy did not move. - With AV on, the PR server's repeat pass also fell (3.383 to 3.279); base's did not (3.373 to 3.364). Compare AL on first or salted passes only. I will look into the drop separately.
---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Per-request draft retention for structured output under PP
commits.pr_body:
Co-authors: @michael-gpu, @tomasruizt 
cc @ArcheyChen 

## Overview

Revert https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442, which introduces a performance regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs, and re-fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54437 by addressing the root cause in `DraftTokensHandler`.

Rework of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61348, rebased, with remaining comments addressed, pre-commit fixed, and simplified implementation + tests.

## Claims

#54442 patched the issue in #54437 by masking out the draft tokens after a handoff race in `DraftTokensHandler`. This fixes #61348 but effectively shortens the draft sequence, causing an acceptance-length (and performance) regression under PP + spec decode with structured outputs.

This PR addresses the `DraftTokensHandler` handoff race directly, fixing the original issue #54437 while maintaining acceptance length.

This PR also adds an E2E repro for #54437 and acceptance length regression.

## Validation

Correctness:

E2E repro in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py`, serves `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` + PP=2 and sends it a mix of constrained and unconstrained requests.

```
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py
```

On main, fails on `_assert_specdec_metrics`, showing a regression in acceptance rate and acceptance length
```
FAILED tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py::test_specdec_pp_structured_output[pp2-tp1] - AssertionError: (0.056471083070452156, 0.08341)
```

After revert #54442, fails on `_assert_outputs_are_structured`, showing unconstrained sampling reported by #54437
```
FAILED tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model/test_structured_output_pp.py::test_specdec_pp_structured_output[pp2-tp1] - AssertionError: ["blue", "
```

This branch
```
1 passed, 3 warning
```

More tests
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output

571 passed, 2 xfailed, 58 warnings

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_draft_tokens_handler.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/draft_model

140 passed, 3 skipped, 19 warnings
```

Performance:

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72

`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark` + 8 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
Ran on H100 80GB.

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ... --pipeline-parallel-size ... --num-repeats 10
```

Results report throughput in tokens/s.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c96: low vs high concurrency
- 95% confidence intervals in brackets

No regression on PP=1

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 673.6 [668.3, 678.9] | 675.7 [666.5, 684.9] | +0.32%
broad / c96 | 9,835.7 [9,749.2, 9,922.2] | 9,785.8 [9,690.9, 9,880.7] | −0.51%
tight / c1 | 1,057.8 [1,047.7, 1,067.9] | 1,062.4 [1,051.7, 1,073.1] | +0.43%
tight / c96 | 18,582.1 [18,469.9, 18,694.3] | 18,565.3 [18,389.4, 18,741.2] | −0.09%

</body></html>

Recover performance regression on PP=2

Case | Main avg [95% CI] | PR avg [95% CI] | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad / c1 | 661.45 [660.82, 662.08] | 662.79 [662.39, 663.19] | +0.20%
broad / c96 | 3,951.12 [3,822.93, 4,079.30] | 12,038.09 [11,768.25, 12,307.93] | +204.68%
tight / c1 | 1,021.45 [1,020.70, 1,022.19] | 1,024.63 [1,023.00, 1,026.26] | +0.31%
tight / c96 | 3,865.53 [3,771.94, 3,959.13] | 21,029.32 [20,574.89, 21,483.75] | +444.02%

</body></html>

## Details

### Background

`DraftTokensHandler` allows workers to asynchronously send draft tokens back to the scheduler / structured output manager for processing.

With async scheduling, it works roughly like:
```
Scheduler-side                          Worker-side
--------------------------------------------------
schedule step N
sample step N
                                        execute step N
schedule step N+1
wait for step N
                                        sample step N
                                        DraftTokensHandler.set_draft_tokens
                                        execute step N+1
DraftTokensHandler.get_draft_tokens
generate sampling bitmasks
sample step N+1
                                        sample step N+1
...
```

On main, `DraftTokensHandler` holds the latest batch set by the worker. This works fine for PP=1, but when PP>=2, this can occur:
```
Scheduler-side          Worker-side
----------------------------------
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch A)
                        set_draft_tokens(micro-batch B)
get_draft_tokens
```

Micro-batch B replaces micro-batch A in the handler. Scheduler-side cannot recover A's drafts and generates incorrect grammar bitmasks, leading to #54437.

#54442 fixes this by effectively truncating the worker-side draft sequence, reducing acceptance length.

This PR fixes this by making `DraftTokensHandler` track draft tokens by request ID. So micro-batch B cannot override micro-batch A.

Final notes:
- Suggest reviewing commits independently
  - `e3595db629d88881e74eafc357e471924b4d9c1f`: revert #54442, could be a separate PR
  - `c67afdec130ca06c6beb5e286a5b83b91fdae3a2`: track draft tokens by request ID.
  - `bb3694db86066ea2d272051b0495bad3ae09d026`: E2E repro
- Alternative #61348 includes adding a debug flag to catch the handoff race, this is not included in this PR in favor of the E2E repro.

---

commits.pr_title: [EPD] Metadata-only image and video inputs for GLM-5.3-Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can now take metadata-only image and video inputs in Python EPD, the same out-of-band placeholder path as Qwen-VL (#50390) and audio models (#57887). The encoder publishes `image_grid_thw`, and for video `video_grid_thw` plus one timestamp per temporal patch. The consumer rebuilds placeholders from those fields and receives embeddings through the EC connector.

No open PR covers this. #61418 is routing-metadata adapters, not EPD media metadata.

## Claims

- An EC consumer no longer reruns GLM-5.3-Flash vision preprocessing when the encoder published the placeholder metadata.
- On a cold 1E+1PD pair this is about 1.14× request throughput and 0.86× TTFT versus forwarding the raw image. The same ratio holds after each arm has warmed its own CUDA graphs.
- On 32 greedy image requests and 16 greedy video requests, prompt token counts and answer text matched the raw-media path on every request. Image and video throughput are separate tables. The image ratio above is not a video result.

## Validation

Not a duplicate of an open PR (search above).

AI assistance was used. The submitting human should review the diff.

Parser contract on the same H200 pod, against the installed tree with this patch (`pytest` 9.1.1, `torchvision` 0.28.0):

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/models/glm5next/test_epd_metadata.py
```

4 passed in 15.54s.

End-to-end on 8× H200, `zai-org` checkpoint `/models/GLM-5.3-Flash` (bf16/fp8), vLLM 0.32.0 plus this patch. The PD worker loads the full checkpoint, 76.5 GiB per TP=4 rank, so the PD side is TP=4 on GPU 4–7. The encoder is a dedicated `ec_producer` and runs encoder-only. In the throughput runs it was also started at TP=4 on GPU 0–3, and each encoder worker loaded 1.17 GiB; a later startup of this patch with `--tensor-parallel-size 1` loaded 1.93 GiB and used 4579 MiB on one GPU. Encoder TP=4 was not required for the vision tower. `ECExampleConnector` over local disk was used because `ECMooncakeConnector` producers require `tensor_parallel_size=1`, and the producer was originally launched with the full-model command. That check does not rule out Mooncake for an encoder-only producer. The tables below were measured with encoder TP=4 and `ECExampleConnector`. Max model len 8192, prefix caching left on for the PD instance, CUDA graphs on, concurrency 64, 64 distinct 768×768 images, 64 output tokens, greedy. Each arm was a fresh process start plus one warmup request, then two measured passes. Zero failed requests. The metadata proxy logged 129 rewrites; the raw proxy (`--no-rewrite`) logged 0.

| arm | pass | req/s | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| raw | cold | 5.46 | 349 | 7575 ms | 59.0 ms |
| raw | warm | 10.91 | 698 | 3573 ms | 31.0 ms |
| metadata-only | cold | 6.22 | 398 | 6530 ms | 50.1 ms |
| metadata-only | warm | 12.51 | 800 | 3076 ms | 26.9 ms |

Logs: the run was on a private pod; the table is the `Serving Benchmark Result` block from `vllm bench serve`.

Video throughput was rerun with `vllm bench serve` after the first 16-request burst proved to be one unschedulable wave (raw warm slower than raw cold, metadata cold dominated by a few multi-second prefills). This run is a different pod, same image and patch. Each arm is a fresh 1E+1PD process and a fresh EC cache. 64 distinct 2-second 320×240 clips at 8 fps, ShareGPT dataset, 64 output tokens, greedy, concurrency 8. One probe measured 248 prompt tokens, and 8192 / 248 caps concurrency at 8. Pass 1 is preceded by 8 warmups of the first clip so Triton JIT is outside the measurement. Pass 2 and pass 3 are repeats with no extra warmup. Zero failed requests. Mean TTFT stays next to the median, and P99 TTFT stays within about 1.5× the mean. The metadata proxy logged 201 rewrites; the raw proxy logged 0. On each paired pass, metadata-only is slightly ahead (about 1.07–1.11× output tok/s and 0.86–0.92× mean TTFT). Repeating a warm pass on the same arm moves output tok/s by 9–12%, which is the same size as that gap, so this table is not a video speedup claim.

| arm | pass | req/s | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| raw | 1 | 4.82 | 308 | 849 ms | 12.8 ms |
| raw | 2 | 6.81 | 436 | 562 ms | 9.7 ms |
| raw | 3 | 6.01 | 385 | 673 ms | 10.4 ms |
| metadata-only | 1 | 5.18 | 331 | 780 ms | 12.1 ms |
| metadata-only | 2 | 7.35 | 471 | 481 ms | 9.6 ms |
| metadata-only | 3 | 6.69 | 428 | 581 ms | 9.7 ms |

Correctness used the same 1E+1PD stack and checkpoint, greedy, `max_tokens=32`, one request at a time. Raw (`--no-rewrite`) first, then metadata-only.

Image: 32 distinct 768×768 images. The metadata proxy logged 32 rewrites.

| image | prompt tokens | answer text |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| match | 32/32 | 32/32 |

Video: 16 distinct 2-second 320×240 clips (8 fps). The metadata proxy logged 16 rewrites. The throughput table above is a separate 64-clip `vllm bench serve` run, not this greedy check.

| video | prompt tokens | answer text |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| match | 16/16 | 16/16 |

Image and video placeholder reconstruction, without a serving stack, is `test_glm5_metadata_only_roundtrip` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py`. On the H200 pod, with this patch and the local `/models/GLM-5.3-Flash` processor:

```bash
python3 -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/models/multimodal/processing \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py \
  -k test_glm5_metadata_only_roundtrip -q
```

2 passed in 24.56s (`image` and `video`). Each case builds the prompt from raw media, publishes the EC metadata, and checks that metadata-only inputs reproduce the same prompt token ids and placeholders.

## Details

`Glm4vMultiModalDataParser.embedding_fields` marks the grid and video timestamps as placeholder metadata and the embeds as values, so `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` drops only the embeds on an EC consumer. Timestamps are computed with the existing GLM-5.3 frame sampler and stored on the processed video item, which is what the encoder publishes and what the prompt replacement reads. Image replacement was already grid-sized; it now works when the request carries only `image_grid_thw`.

Video still needs those timestamps because a GLM placeholder includes one timestamp string per temporal patch, not only `grid.prod()`. Requests that omit the metadata stay on the raw-media path.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Count tool call deltas as generated tokens in vllm-bench openai-responses
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust `vllm-bench` `openai-responses` backend marks every tool-call-only response as failed. It counts only `output_text` and `reasoning_text` deltas as tokens, and a forced tool call streams only `function_call_arguments` deltas. This counts the four tool delta events the vLLM Responses server emits. #62753 is the same fix for the Python `vllm bench serve` client.

## Claims

- 100 tool calls the server completed with HTTP 200 went from 0 to 100 successful.
- Added events: `function_call_arguments`, `custom_tool_call_input`, `mcp_call_arguments`, `code_interpreter_call_code` (from `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/streaming_events.py`). Tool arguments are timed but not added to `generated_text`.

## Validation

Two new tests in `openai_responses.rs`: a tool-call-only response (TTFT, ITL, latency, usage) and each tool delta type on its own. Both fail with the old match arm. `cargo test -p vllm-bench` passes (215), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

RTX 3080, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, 100 prompts, concurrency 16, `tool_choice: "required"` via `--extra-body`:

| | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| completed / failed | 0 / 100 | 100 / 0 |
| total generated tokens | 0 | 2,090 |

The 2,090 output tokens match the Python bench on the same workload.

## Details

The backend came in with #59489. Leaving tool calls out fails the request, so tool-calling workloads such as BFCL can't be measured with it.

No issue or PR covers this. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write the change and tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and GPU comparison.
